applyColourScheme.name: applyColourScheme
applyColourScheme.description: Put `scheme` on `root` (the `<html>` element by default): its class from `schemes` (default `dark` for dark and none for light), the other scheme's class taken off, and `color-scheme` so native controls and scrollbars follow.
applyColourScheme.signature: applyColourScheme(scheme: ColourScheme, root?: HTMLElement, schemes?: ColourSchemeClasses): void

AppShell.name: AppShell
AppShell.description:
The page frame: it paints the page canvas and sets the type face, ink and font smoothing
(`antialiased`), so an app writes no page-background or font rule of its own (a theme remaps
the canvas and the font stacks). A sticky one-row header, an optional second `subnav` row, the main area and an
optional footer. Header, main and footer each sit in a `Container`, so pages never set their own
width or padding. `bleed` drops main's Container (the header keeps its own), for a layout that
needs the whole width (`FullBleedLayout`). Main is a flex column. `SidebarLayout` needs no
`bleed`: its rail and canvas share the header's Container.

The header row is laid out by its slots, left to right: `brand`, `nav`, then `header` (anything
the slots do not cover), then `controls`, pushed to the end. An app writes no wrapper or
styling for any of them: an item that only fits a wide screen goes in a `Show from`. A bar
that sticks under the header as the page scrolls is a `StickyBar`.

On a phone (below `md`) the header is one 56px row at every page: `brand`, `header`, `controls`
and a "Menu" button (`menuLabel`), and `nav` and `subnav` move into that menu, so every link is
reachable and nothing scrolls sideways. The menu is the browser's popover (`popovertarget`), so
it works with the keyboard, closes on Escape and a click outside, hands focus back to the button,
and opens on a page that never hydrates. From `md` the header is the
row, and the `subnav` row, as they are, except that a `nav` too wide for the row folds into the
Menu and comes back when the screen is wide enough (measured, with script; a `subnav` never
folds, it scrolls sideways with a fade).

The edges need nothing from the app: with `viewport-fit=cover` every Container clears the
safe-area insets at the sides, the header the top one and the shell the bottom one; and an
element with an `id` anywhere inside lands below the sticky header when a link or focus scrolls
to it.

`controls` stay in the row at every width, so keep them few (a theme toggle, the viewer's avatar);
on a phone a crowded `controls` clips, and the Menu button is never the part cut off. Pickers and
actions that do not fit a phone row go in `menuControls`: rendered once, from `md` they sit at the
row's end, before `header` and `controls`, and fold into the Menu with a `nav` that does not fit;
below `md` they are at the foot of the Menu, after `nav` and `subnav`. The markup is in the order
the row shows, so the focus moves as the eye does.

props.name: bleed
props.description:
Main without a Container, for a full-bleed layout.

For a layout that needs the whole width, such as `FullBleedLayout`; `SidebarLayout` needs no
`bleed`.

props.name: brand
props.description: The brand: a logo and a name, in the header's brand type, with the gap between them. `AppShellBrand` makes both one link.

props.name: controls
props.description: The end of the row: a picker, a theme toggle. Gap-2, vertically centred; no child shrinks, and a full-width control (a `Select` at its default) sizes to its content.

props.name: density
props.description:
The app's type step, set once here and nowhere else: `compact` sets text, headings and controls
one step down everywhere inside, for an app's dense chrome. Left out, text is 16px, as a site's.

props.name: footer
props.description: The page footer: small muted text in a `Container`, under a hairline. Hidden in print with `printChrome={false}`.

props.name: header
props.description:
The escape hatch: a free node in the header row, after `brand` and `nav`.

Only for a node no other slot covers: prefer `brand`, `nav` and `controls`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: menuControls
props.description:
Pickers and actions that do not fit a phone row, such as a project `Select` and a Sign out
`Button`. From `md` they sit at the row's end, before `header` and `controls`, and fold into the
Menu with the `nav`; below `md` they are at the foot of the Menu, after `nav` and `subnav`.
Rendered once, so a field keeps its state and ids stay unique.
`controls` stay in the row at every width, so keep those few.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description:
The phone menu button's name, for an app in another language. Only drawn below `md`, and only
when `nav`, `subnav` or `menuControls` is given.

props.name: nav
props.description: The main navigation, e.g. a `Tabs` of links (it is already a `<nav>`). Below `md` it is in the menu.

props.name: printChrome
props.description:
Whether a print shows the header and footer. `false` prints only the page: the header and
footer are hidden, and main's Container drops its padding (the page margin is then `@page`'s).

The screen is unchanged.

props.name: skipLabel
props.description:
The skip link's words, for an app in another language. The link is the page's first tab stop,
hidden until it has the focus, and moves the focus past the header to the main area.

props.name: subnav
props.description: A second fixed-height row under the header from `md`, e.g. a `Tabs` of links. Below `md` it is in the menu with `nav`.

AppShellBrand.name: AppShellBrand
AppShellBrand.description:
The `brand` slot as one link: a logo and a label inside the same `<a>`, so the whole brand is the
way home. The label names the link; the logo is decoration and hidden from assistive tech.
`collapse` shows only the logo below `sm`, the label staying in the accessible name. An in-app
`href` is drawn by the app's router link through `LinkProvider`.

props.name: collapse
props.description: Below `sm` only the logo shows; the label is visually hidden and still names the link. Needs a `logo`.

props.name: href
props.description:
Where the brand links, usually the app's home (`/`).

With a router it goes through the app's `LinkProvider`, like every link.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The name beside the logo. It is the link's accessible name.

props.name: logo
props.description: The mark before the label, e.g. an `Avatar` or an ``.

props.name: logoSize
props.description: The logo slot's box: sm 20px, md 24px (the default, an `Avatar size="sm"`), lg 32px. An `` or `

appShellRootClassFor.name: appShellRootClassFor
appShellRootClassFor.description:
Everything an app puts on its own `<html>` from the scheme the server knows: that scheme's class
(`schemeClass`) and the shell's root class, joined: `<html className={appShellRootClassFor(scheme,
schemes)}>`.

Audio.name: Audio
Audio.description:
An `<audio>` with the browser's own controls, at one fixed size: 20rem wide, narrower only when its column is. It loads
metadata only, and lazily where the browser can, so the page does not pull the file until it is
played. A voice note or a clip has no visible title, so `label` names the player. `src` is the
app's own file; `children` is the fallback for a browser that cannot play it.

props.name: children
props.description: The text for a browser that cannot play it.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the player for a screen reader, as "Voice note from Anna": audio has no visible title.

props.name: src
props.description: The audio file, the app's own.

Avatar.name: Avatar
Avatar.description:
A person as a round badge of initials, or as their photo when `src` is given; `shape="square"`
marks an org or a team instead. It never loads a remote image on its own: that is a request to
another server for decoration, and it makes a screenshot depend on the network. `src` is the
app's own local path. With `onClick` the whole Avatar is one button, with `href` one link. A row of overlapping avatars
is an `AvatarStack`. While `loading` with an empty `name` it is a bone of its size and shape.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the Avatar one link, named by `name`; an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: name
props.description: Whose avatar: its initials, its colour (a hash of the name) and its title or `alt`.

props.name: onClick
props.description:
Makes the Avatar one button, named by `name`: a person who opens their profile or a menu.
Without it (or `href`) the Avatar is a plain mark.

props.name: shape
props.description:
`round` for a person; `square` (rounded corners) for an org or a team, so the two never read
as each other.

props.name: size
props.description: `xs` 16px, `sm` 24px, `md` 32px, `lg` 40px, `xl` 56px, `2xl` 64px or `3xl` 96px.

props.name: src
props.description:
The person's photo, a local path. It replaces the initials and is announced as `name`. If it
fails to load, the initials show instead.

AvatarStack.name: AvatarStack
AvatarStack.description:
Members as a row of overlapping avatars, each in a ring in the page colour that separates it from
the next. With `max`, the first `max` show and a "+N" chip of the same size and shape stands for
the rest. The row is one image to assistive tech, named by the people in it. While `loading`
with no `items` yet it draws three avatar bones.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: Who is in the stack, in order. Give each person's full name, as for `Avatar`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: max
props.description: How many avatars show before a "+N" chip takes the rest. Without it every person shows.

props.name: shape
props.description: `square` for a stack of orgs or teams, as `Avatar`'s `shape`.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of every avatar and of the chip, as `Avatar`'s `size`.

Badge.name: Badge
Badge.description:
A small red count, 10px, for sitting on an icon. Its size is in rem and its height grows with
its line, so it scales with the reader's text size instead of clipping. An icon with a count is an `IconButton` with
its `count`, which pins the Badge to its corner and puts the count in the button's name. A
count above 99 reads `99+`. While `loading` it is
a bone of its size: a count is a number, so 0 is a value and not a gap.

props.name: corner
props.description: Pin it to the top corner at the end edge of its `relative` parent, over the icon.

props.name: count
props.description: The number shown; above 99 it reads `99+`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

BottomSheet.name: BottomSheet
BottomSheet.description:
A non-modal panel docked to the bottom edge of its positioned parent, over a full-screen view (a
map, a canvas) that stays usable behind it. It rests at one of its `snaps`; the handle steps
through them (Enter and Space; ArrowUp and ArrowDown one up or down), a drag of the handle moves
it and releases to the nearest snap (a fling steps on), and Escape inside it returns it to the
first. Nothing is made inert and focus never moves. Full width below `md`, a panel at the start
edge from `md` up, or, with `inlineFrom`, plain content in the page from that width.

props.name: children
props.description: The scrolling body.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions pinned under the scrolling body.

props.name: header
props.description: The row under the handle: a heading and a count. It stays put while the body scrolls.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: inlineFrom
props.description:
From this width up the sheet is no sheet: its header, body and footer sit in the page's flow
with no handle, no snaps and no height of its own, so the parent's grid places it (a list
column beside a map). Below it, it is the sheet. One tree, switched by CSS: nothing renders
twice, so `onHeightChange` still reports the snap's height: there the view has nothing under
the list to pad. Without it the sheet is a panel at the start edge from `md` up.

props.name: label
props.description: The sheet's accessible name, as a region, and its handle button's.

props.name: onHeightChange
props.description:
Called with the sheet's height (px): on mount, on every change of `snap`, when the parent
resizes, and on every move of a drag, so a map camera padded by it follows the finger.

props.name: onSnapChange
props.description: Called with the snap to move to: from the handle, a drag, or Escape (back to 0). Set `snap` here.

props.name: snap
props.description: The current snap, an index into `snaps`. Render the first (0) first and a page with no JavaScript shows it.

props.name: snaps
props.description:
The heights it rests at, lowest first, at least two: a number from 0 to 1 is a share of the
parent's height, a `"120px"` string is pixels. A snap taller than the parent is held at its height.

Breadcrumbs.name: Breadcrumbs
Breadcrumbs.description:
`org / project / build / snapshot`: the last crumb is the current page. A crumb is a node, or a
`Crumb` object when it links. A trail too long for its row wraps onto the next line; a long parent
truncates, showing its whole label in a tooltip on hover, focus and a tap, and the current page is
never cut: its words wrap instead.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The trail, first to current: a node, or a `Crumb` (`{ label, href, external? }`) for one that links. The last is the current page; a `Crumb` there links to it with `aria-current="page"`.

props.name: label
props.description: The trail's accessible name, on its `<nav>`, for an app in another language.

BulletItem.name: BulletItem
BulletItem.description:
One item of a `BulletList`: an `<li>` in the body text's size and ink (the long-form scale inside
a `Prose`). A long unbroken string (a URL, a token) breaks at the edge instead of overflowing.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

BulletList.name: BulletList
BulletList.description:
A bulleted `<ul>`: discs, indented, a small gap between items. `ordered` makes it a numbered
`<ol>` (steps a reader follows in order), with the same indent and gap. Its children are `BulletItem`s.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: ordered
props.description: A numbered `<ol>` instead of the bulleted `<ul>`, for items whose order matters.

Button.name: Button
Button.description:
A button in the primary, outline, ghost, link or dashed style (the link has no box: text with an
underline on hover, for an in-line action; `dashed` is the full-width "add" row, a dashed
outline with muted text that fills its container). `icon` puts an `Icon` before the label.
`size="sm"` is compact and `size="lg"` larger, `size={{ base: "md", md: "lg" }}` changes at 48rem,
and with no `size` it takes its container's;
`tone="positive"` is green and `tone="danger"` is red;
`pressed` makes it a toggle: neutral when off, the tone's fill when on. `count` puts a small
number chip after the label; the chip is part of the name, and a button that opens something
also takes `aria-expanded`.
Defaults to `type="button"`. `disabledReason` and `busy` are the two disabled states that say
more than a plain `disabled`, which keeps its half-opacity look; `busy="Saving"` also swaps the
label. `ref` reaches the `<button>` or the `<a>`. `href` makes it a link instead,
with the same look (the app's router link through `LinkProvider` for an in-app path, else a plain
`<a>`; `external` opens a new tab).

props.name: busy
props.description:
The work is in flight: disabled, `aria-busy`, keeps its colour. Wins over `disabledReason`. A
string is also the label while busy, in place of the children: `busy={saving && "Saving"}`.

props.name: count
props.description:
A small number in a chip after the label: how many are behind the button (the splits a row
has, the comments on a thread). It is part of the button's name, "Splits, 3", and `0` is
shown. For a button that opens something, also pass `aria-expanded`.

Pass `aria-controls` for what it opens too; the caller owns that state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button; say why with `disabledReason` instead where there is a reason.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description:
Why the button cannot be pressed: greys it flat and blocks it (`aria-disabled`, its click,
Enter and Space do nothing) while it stays in the tab order, and shows the reason as its
tooltip on hover, keyboard focus and a tap, read out as its description.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the button a link to this URL; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon from the `Icon` set before the label, decorative, at the button's size.

props.name: pressed
props.description:
A toggle: sets `aria-pressed`. On `outline` and `ghost`, `false` draws the neutral off look
and `true` the tone's primary fill, so a row of filter chips shows the selected one plainly.
Left out, the button is not a toggle, has no `aria-pressed` and keeps its variant's look.

props.name: ref
props.type: ((instance: HTMLButtonElement | null) => void | (() => VoidOrUndefinedOnly)) | RefObject<HTMLButtonElement | null> | ((instance: HTMLAnchorElement | null) => void | (() => VoidOrUndefinedOnly)) | RefObject<...> | null
props.description: Reaches the `<button>`, or the `<a>` of a link button, to focus it or measure it.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is compact, for table rows and toolbars; `lg` is larger, for a hero call to action. Left
out, a Button takes the size of the `Card`, `ListRow` or `Table` it sits in, else `md`.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS: `md` on a phone,
`lg` from 48rem up.

The first load paints the right size. Give every control in the row the same value, so it stays
aligned.

props.name: tone
props.description:
`positive` is green, for accept and approve; `danger` is red, for delete and clear. Not for
`dashed`, which has the one look.

props.name: type
props.description: `"button"` by default; `"submit"` submits the form the button is in.

props.name: variant
props.description:
`primary` is filled, for the one main action; `outline` and `ghost` are quieter; `link` is
text with an underline on hover; `dashed` is an "add another" row that fills its container.

ButtonGroup.name: ButtonGroup
ButtonGroup.description:
A wrapping row of buttons with one optional item pushed to the far end (a Back link, say). On a
narrow viewport the row wraps and `end` stays at the end of the last line. `label` makes it a
named `role="group"`. Directly in a `Card` footer it spans the footer, so `end` reaches the far
edge.

props.name: end
props.description: One item, pushed to the end of the row.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the group: sets `role="group"` and `aria-label`.

Callout.name: Callout
Callout.description:
A tinted notice box, with an optional bold title above its body. Its text is text-sm (text-base/7
inside a `Prose`, boxed or `banner`). `actions` puts a button or link
at the end of the row, or under the text at full width below `sm`; `banner` makes it a flat strip (bottom border only, no radius) for the
top of a `Card flush` and nowhere else: a padded card or a padded `FullBleedLayout` column
would inset it. `align="center"` centres the text. In a page's column the notice is a plain Callout, first in the column's `Stack`. With `actions` the box is `relative`, so a `TextLink
stretch` there makes the whole callout its click target, like a link in a table row. `icon`
sets one of the library's icons at the start of the box, in the tone's ink. `danger` is
`role="alert"` and `warn` is `role="status"`, so a screen reader announces them when they
appear; the other tones have no role.

props.name: actions
props.description: A button or link at the end of the row, beside the title and body; on a phone, under them at full width.

props.name: align
props.description:
`center` centres the title and body, for a success that stands alone. With
`actions` only the text is centred.

props.name: banner
props.description: A flat strip: `border-b` only and no radius, for the top of a `Card flush` only.

props.name: icon
props.description: One of the library's icons, at the start of the box beside the text.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: A bold line above the body.

props.name: tone
props.description:
What the notice means: `neutral` a plain note, `info` something worth knowing, `positive` a
result, `warn` a thing to check before going on, `danger` a failure or something that cannot
be undone.

Caption.name: Caption
Caption.description:
Fine print / metadata. A paragraph (`p`; `as="span"` inline), text-sm/5 normal, tertiary
(text-xs/4 under an `AppShell density="compact"`). Takes `tone`,
`numeric`, `mono`, `lines` and `align` like `Text`, and `italic` for a muted hint and `breakWords`
for a long unbroken string such as a URL.

props.name: align
props.description:
Set the text at `start`, `center` or `end` of its block. The run becomes block-level, so the
alignment has a box to act on (a table header cell, a right-hand column).

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; each role has a semantic default.

props.name: breakWords
props.description: Break a long unbroken string (a URL, a token) where the container ends, instead of overflowing.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: italic
props.description: Italic: a muted hint or a caption.

props.name: lines
props.description:
Show at most this many lines (1 to 4) and end in an ellipsis: `1` cuts the run where its
container ends, `2` to `4` wrap and stop. With plain-text content the full text becomes the
`title`. A "Show all" toggle is the app's own state: `lines={open ? undefined : 3}`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: The monospace face, for an id, a path or a command.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures, so a column of amounts lines up.

props.name: title
props.description: The full text on hover, for a run that `lines` cuts and whose content is not plain text.

props.name: tone
props.description:
The ink: `neutral`, the default, is the role's own; `muted` and `accent` set the hierarchy of
the text; `positive`, `warn`, `danger` and `info` say what a run means (see `TextTone`).

Card.name: Card
Card.description:
A bordered panel with an optional title, count and status. A titled card is an `article` named by
its title, one with only an `aria-label` an `article` too, and any other a `div`. Two opt-in forms
for data views: `flush` drops the padding and clips the corners, for a table that runs edge to
edge; `bar` puts the title, count and `actions` in a tinted strip across the top, over the body.
A flush card has no padding for a `title`, so give it a `bar`. An empty state is an `EmptyState`,
which draws its own dashed frame. Inside a card a `Stack` is `xs` apart, and the title's
heading level is one below the heading that holds the card. `size="sm"` is the dense padding and `size="lg"` the
roomy one, the same on a `ListRow` and a `FileDrop`. `tone` is the Callout's set, for a data panel that carries a status
(a soft fill and border, no shadow); a message is still a `Callout`, and `bar` has no tone. `hue`
paints one of a set of peer cards in its own hue, the theme's; it is not a status, and `tone`,
`bar` and `dashed` win over it. `dashed` draws a dashed edge for a card that stands for something
not real yet, and with `bar` the strip's edge is dashed too. `width="sm"` caps the card at 24rem. A
titled panel is named by its title: the root gets
`aria-labelledby` pointing at the heading, unless the caller passes its own `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`, which wins. Other props (`id`, `data-*`, `aria-*`) go on the root. The root is `relative`, so a
`TextLink stretch` inside it covers the card. A card with an `id` is an anchor target: `#id`
scrolls it clear of the sticky header (and a `subnav`) and outlines it in the accent colour while
it is the target.

`icon` is one of the library's icons at feature size in the accent colour, above the title: the
mark of a feature card. It sits in the padded body, so `bar` and `flush` have none.

`footer` is a tinted strip across the bottom, under a hairline, for the card's own actions or a
total; in a `CardGrid` it stays at the foot of a card that is stretched to the row's height. It
suits a panel, not a card that is a link.

`fill` makes a panel take its parent's full height (the parent sets it): the title or bar and the
`inset` band stay put and the body scrolls, with room inside it for a focus ring at its edge. Not
on a link card.

`href` makes the whole card one link: a hover border and the focus ring, with the link stretched
over the card, so it takes no `actions` or `footer`. `onPress` makes it one button the same way. A
`TextLink`, `Button` or `Checkbox` in the body sits above the link and is clickable on its own. An
in-app `href` is drawn by the app's router link through `LinkProvider`. `external` opens it in a
new tab, and `more` draws a "Read more" line at its foot. On a link or button card `id`, `data-*`
and the describing `aria-*` (`aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, …) go on the card root; the
control's own `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-current` and `aria-pressed` stay on it. The
link or button is named by the card's title; an untitled one by the card's text, through the root's
id, which is generated when the caller gives none.

In a `CardGrid align="regions"` the card's header, body and footer line up with its neighbours'
across the row.

While `loading` a card with no children draws three lines of text bones, a `flush` one three
`ListRow` bones; what it has (its title, its children) draws as usual.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons or links at the end of the header: in the strip with `bar`, else beside the title.

props.name: attention
props.description:
The warn tone's strong border in place of the card's own, for the one card in a set that needs
a look (a run that differed). It keeps the card's fill. Name why in the card too (a `Pill` in
`badge`, or the body); the border alone says nothing to a screen reader.

Add `tone="warn"` for the warn surface too.

props.name: badge
props.description:
A `Pill` (or any small node) pinned in the top corner at the end edge, over the content and
inside the radius, with no change to the layout. On a titled link card the link is named by the
title alone; an untitled one is named by its whole content, badge included. A link or button in
it is clickable on its own.

Use it for a category (`Pill tone="info"`) or a flag on the thing itself.

props.name: bar
props.description: Put the title, count and actions in a tinted strip above the body, edge to edge.

props.name: count
props.description: A small number beside the title (how many rows the card holds). Needs a `title`.

props.name: dashed
props.description:
A dashed edge, for a card that stands for something not real yet: a plan, a draft, an imagined
result beside a real one. With `bar` the strip's lower edge is dashed too.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: fill
props.description:
Take the parent's full height: the title or bar stays put and the body scrolls. The parent sets
the height.

For a panel in a fixed-height layout, such as a sheet over a map. Put links or controls in the
body, so a keyboard can reach and scroll it.

props.name: flush
props.description: No padding and `overflow-hidden`: the body (a table, a list) fills the card.

props.name: footer
props.description: A tinted strip across the bottom of the card, under a hairline, for the card's own actions or a total. It stays at the foot when the card is stretched in a `CardGrid`.

props.name: href
props.description:
Makes the whole card one link to this URL, with no `actions` or `footer`; an in-app path goes
through the app's `LinkProvider`. The link is named by the card's title.

props.name: hue
props.description:
One hue of a set of peer cards, such as one card per product: a soft fill and edge the theme
paints. It is not a status (that is `tone`), and the title still names the card. Ignored with
`bar` and `dashed`.

props.name: icon
props.description:
One of the library's icons, drawn at feature size in the accent colour above the title: the
mark of a feature card. Ignored with `bar` and `flush`.

Pick it by the idea it stands for.

props.name: inset
props.description:
A band across the card, edge to edge inside its padding, under the title and above the
children: a `ProgressBar` or a strip of colour that runs the card's full width.

A bordered sub-card inside a card is a nested `Card tone="neutral"`, not a hand-built box.

props.name: level
props.default: one below the heading that holds the card: 2 on the page, 3 in a `Section`
props.description: The title's heading level, 2 to 6. It does not change how the title looks.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: more
props.description:
A "Read more" line with an arrow at the foot of the card, in the accent colour: the cue that the
card goes somewhere, for a post or an article. Draw it on every card of a set or on none.

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: The words of the `more` line.

props.name: onPress
props.description:
Makes the whole card one button that runs this, stretched over the card like a link card's link
and named by its title: a card the user picks (a store, a plan). With no `actions`, `footer` or
`href`. A picked card says so with `aria-pressed` and its own words (a `Pill` in `badge`).

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is dense padding on the body, heading and bar, and makes a `Button`, `IconButton` or `Pill`
inside with no `size` of its own `sm` too; `lg` is one step roomier than `md`.

`sm` suits a dense dashboard, `lg` a card that stands alone.

props.name: status
props.description: A `Pill` (or any node) directly beside the title and count, not at the far end like `actions`. Needs a `title`.

props.name: title
props.description: The card's heading (a small uppercase label unless `titleStyle` says otherwise). It names the card, which is then an `article`.

props.name: titleStyle
props.description:
How the `title` is set. `overline` is the small uppercase label of a panel; `name` is the same
heading in sentence case and the primary ink, for a card whose title is a name (a shop, a listing,
an event). Count, status, actions, `bar` and `size` work the same with both.

props.name: tone
props.description: A soft fill and border in the Callout's tones, for a data panel with a status. Ignored with `bar`.

props.name: width
props.description:
`sm` caps the card at 24rem, for a card that stands alone in a wide column (a sign-in panel, a
plan). Left out, the card takes the width it is given.

CardGrid.name: CardGrid
CardGrid.description:
A responsive grid of tiles of one width: one column on a phone, two from `sm`, `columns` from `lg`.
A main area beside a narrower one is not a grid of tiles: it is `SideColumn` (`asideWidth="third"`
for two thirds and one). `columns="auto"` instead fits as many per row as the width allows, each at least `minWidth` wide:
`md` (17rem, the default) or `sm` (12rem). `align="start"` keeps each card its own height
instead of stretching it to the tallest in its row; `align="regions"` lines up each card's header,
body and footer across the row (CSS subgrid). `minColumns={2}` keeps two tiles to a row on a
phone. Every cell has `min-w-0`, so a truncating name inside a card cuts instead of widening its
column. A `CardGridRow` spans every column. `as="ul"` makes it a list of cards for a
screen reader: the grid is a `<ul>` and each child is wrapped in an `<li>`, still stretched.
With no children it draws `empty` (an `EmptyState`) in place of the grid. While `loading` with
none it draws one card of bones per column (three for `auto`), never `empty`.

props.name: align
props.description:
`start` keeps each card its own height; the default stretches every card to the tallest in its
row. `regions` stretches them too and lines up each card's header, body and footer with its
neighbours' across the row, so titles of different lengths do not push the bodies out of line.

props.name: as
props.description: `ul` makes the grid a list: each child is wrapped in an `<li>`. Default `div`.

props.name: columns
props.description: Cards per row from `lg` (one on a phone, two from `sm`), or `auto` for as many as fit.

props.name: empty
props.description: Drawn in place of the grid when there are no children: an `EmptyState`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: minColumns
props.description:
The fewest cards in a row: `2` keeps two small tiles side by side on a phone (products in a
shop), where the default is one.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: With `columns="auto"`, the narrowest a card gets: `md` 17rem or `sm` 12rem.

CardGridRow.name: CardGridRow
CardGridRow.description:
One item that spans every column of a `CardGrid`: a heading over a group of cards, or one wide
card in the run (an announcement among products). In `as="ul"` its `<li>` spans the row. It takes
no `align="regions"` rows: what it holds keeps its own layout.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

CartButton.name: CartButton
CartButton.description:
The header's cart: the bag icon, how many things are in it and, with `total`, what they come to.
It is one ghost button that opens the cart (a `Drawer`), so pass `aria-expanded` and
`aria-controls` with the drawer's state; with `href` it is a link to the cart page instead. A
screen reader hears it as "Cart, 2 items, R480": the label, the count in words and the total.
The count is drawn whatever it is, `0` included, so the header does not shift as things go in.

props.name: count
props.description: How many things are in the cart; `0` is shown.

props.name: href
props.description: The cart's own page, in place of a drawer; an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: itemsLabel
props.description: The count in words, for a screen reader, in an app's own language.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's name before the count.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Opens the cart; pass `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` for the drawer it opens.

props.name: total
props.description: What they come to, formatted by the app ("R480"). Left out, only the count shows.

CenteredLayout.name: CenteredLayout
CenteredLayout.description: A narrow card (`max-w-md`) centred in the Container at a fixed offset from the top, for sign-in, landing, not-found and error pages. The one layout that does not share the start edge. While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted line under the title.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mark
props.description: Drawn first in the card, above the title, e.g. a large status numeral. Not a heading.

props.name: title
props.description: The card's `h1`.

ChatComposer.name: ChatComposer
ChatComposer.description:
The box a message is typed into, with its button beside it. It keeps its own text, and the box
grows with it from 2 rows to 8. Enter sends the trimmed text and clears the box; Shift+Enter is a
newline. Send stays enabled on an empty box: sending empty or whitespace-only text sends nothing
and shows `emptyReason` under the box until the next keystroke. While `busy` a reply is on its way: the button is Stop, Enter does not send, and typing
carries on with the text kept for the next send.

props.name: busy
props.description:
A reply is on its way: the button is Stop and Enter does not send. With no `onStop`, the button
stays a disabled Send and no Stop is drawn.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the box and the button. For a chat that cannot take a message at all, not for a reply in flight: that is `busy`.

props.name: emptyReason
props.description: Shown under the box when Send is pressed on an empty box.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The box's name for assistive tech; it is not drawn.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Called with the trimmed text.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called when the reader presses Stop.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The hint inside the empty box.

props.name: sendLabel
props.description: The button's word, for sending.

props.name: stopLabel
props.description: The button's word, while `busy`.

ChatMessage.name: ChatMessage
ChatMessage.description:
One message in a chat: a bubble on the sender's side, with an optional line above it and a row of
actions under it. `children` is the body as the caller wants it (plain text, which keeps its line
breaks, a `Markdown`, an `Image`). `streaming` marks a reply still arriving; with no children it
draws the caret alone, the pending state.

props.name: actions
props.description: A row under the bubble on the message's own side: copy, retry, a row of reaction `Pill`s.

props.name: author
props.description: Who sent it, read first by a screen reader and drawn nowhere: alignment alone tells a screen reader nothing. Show a sender with `meta`.

props.name: children
props.description: The body. It may be empty while `streaming`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: meta
props.description: A small line above the bubble: a sender and a time, already formatted.

props.name: role
props.description: Whose side it sits on: `user` on the right on the inset fill, `assistant` on the left on the surface.

props.name: streaming
props.description:
The reply is still arriving: sets `aria-busy` and draws a caret after the body, which pulses
unless the reader asks for reduced motion.

ChatThread.name: ChatThread
ChatThread.description:
The scrolling box of a chat: its children are the messages, tool cards and anything else, a gap
apart. It follows the newest content unless the reader has scrolled up. It is a named region and
a tab stop, so a keyboard can scroll it. It is deliberately not a live region, which would read
every streamed token aloud: set `announce` when a message is finished.

props.name: announce
props.description: Text a screen reader reads out politely when it changes. Set it when a message is finished, not on each token.

props.name: empty
props.description: Drawn instead when there are no children: an `EmptyState`.

props.name: height
props.description:
The tallest it gets before it scrolls: `sm` 20rem, `md` 28rem, `lg` 40rem. `fill` takes the
height of a parent that sets one.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the region.

Checkbox.name: Checkbox
Checkbox.description:
A checkbox with its label. It is a real `<input type="checkbox">`, drawn by the library (an
empty outlined box, then a filled accent one with a check mark) so it reads the same in every
theme and browser. Every prop but the label goes on the input, and `ref` reaches it.
`size="sm"` is `text-xs` and a smaller box, for a dense row; `size="lg"` is `text-base` and a
larger box. Leave `label` out for a bare box in a table cell, and name it with `aria-label`. The
box sits on the label's first line, so a label that wraps reads from the box. `hint` is a muted
line under the label that says more, like a `Field`'s; `error` adds a red line under it, with an alert
icon, and makes the box `aria-invalid` and red-edged. The note is the box's `aria-describedby`.
`onChange` gets the new checked state; take `checked` with it, or `defaultChecked` alone.
`indeterminate` draws a dash for a select-all box over a partly chosen list. `variant="card"`
draws it as an option card: a bordered box with the label as its title and the hint under it. Under a finger the
hit area grows to 44px.
While `loading` the label is drawn and the box is a bone of its size.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description:
Why the box cannot be changed: it dims and is blocked (`aria-disabled`; a click and Space
change nothing) while it stays in the tab order, and the reason is its tooltip on hover,
keyboard focus and a tap, read out as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A red line under the hint, with an alert icon, announced politely; makes the box `aria-invalid`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the label that says more. It is the box's `aria-describedby`.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description:
Mixed: some of what the box stands for is chosen and some is not, as a select-all box over a
partly chosen list. It draws a dash and is read as "mixed"; a click checks it. The caller owns
it: work it out from the list on every render.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the box. Leave it out for a bare box (a table cell) and name it with `aria-label`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new checked state when the person ticks or clears the box.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<input>`, for focus control.

props.name: size
props.description: The label's text size and the box with it.

props.name: variant
props.description:
`plain` is the box and its words. `card` puts them in a bordered box the width of its parent,
the label a title and the `hint` its description: for a few options that each need a line of
explaining. The whole card is the click target, and a ticked one takes an accent edge.

Cluster.name: Cluster
Cluster.description:
A horizontal row of items a fixed `gap` apart (`sm` by default): the row counterpart of `Stack`. `align` is the cross axis (`center` default, `baseline` for mixed text sizes, `start`, `end`) and `justify` the main one (`start` default, `between` to push the first and last items to the two ends, `end`). The items flow onto further lines when the row runs out of room; `wrap={false}` keeps them on one line. Put one `ClusterGrow` around the item that takes the room left over, an input beside its buttons, say. An empty `ClusterGrow` is a spacer that pushes what follows it to the end. `ButtonGroup` is the row for buttons; use `Cluster` for any other row. `as="span"` is for a row inside phrasing content, such as a `PageHeader` description (a `

`): its items must be phrasing content too, so no `ClusterGrow`. `as="ul"` or `as="ol"` is a wrapping list with no markers (tags, chips), as in `CardGrid`: the Cluster wraps each child in its own `

  • `, so the caller writes the items (`Pill`s) and never an `
  • `. `as="nav"` is a row of links (a footer's or a section's): a `
    ` named by its required `aria-label`, holding a list with each link in its own `
  • `.

props.name: align
props.description: The cross axis: `center`, `baseline` (for mixed text sizes), `start` or `end`.

props.name: as
props.description:
The element: `div`, `span` for a row inside a `

` or other phrasing content, `ul` or `ol` for a list (no markers; the Cluster wraps each child in an `

  • `), or `nav` for a row of links (a `
    ` named by `aria-label`, around such a list). In a `span` the items must be phrasing content, so no `ClusterGrow`.

props.name: gap
props.description:
The space between items: the first steps of the gap scale. Its default is one of those the
`Size` type lists as not `md`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: justify
props.description: The main axis: `start`, `center`, `between` (the first and last items at the two ends) or `end`.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Let the items flow onto further lines when the row runs out of room. `false` keeps them on one line.

ClusterGrow.name: ClusterGrow
ClusterGrow.description:
The one child of a `Cluster` (or of a `Stack` with `rowFrom`) that grows to the room left in the
row. By default it can shrink to nothing (`min-w-0`), so the items beside it stay on the line and
a long value truncates instead of pushing them out. With `minWidth` it instead keeps that width
(`sm` 12rem, `md` 17rem) and, in a `Cluster` with `wrap`, drops onto the next line when the room
left is narrower, rather than being squashed. Empty, it is a spacer.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: The narrowest it gets: `sm` 12rem or `md` 17rem. In a `Cluster` with `wrap` it wraps under the other items below this width. Left out, it shrinks to nothing.

Code.name: Code
Code.description:
Inline code: mono, on a subtle inset background. It takes the surrounding text colour and size (a
touch smaller, for the mono face). `lines={1}` keeps a long value (a hash, a path) on one line,
cut with an ellipsis, and shows its whole text in a tooltip while it is cut; `breakWords` instead breaks a long unbroken
value at the edge of its box, as `Text` does.

props.name: breakWords
props.description: Breaks a long unbroken value (a URL, a hash) at the edge of its box.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: lines
props.description: `1` keeps it on one line, cut with an ellipsis; while it is cut, its whole text shows in a tooltip.

CodeBlock.name: CodeBlock
CodeBlock.description:
A block of code: mono, in a bordered inset box. No client JS unless `copy` adds a copy button
beside the code, which copies it exactly as given. `language` colours
it: `tsx`, `ts`, `js`, `json`, `bash`, `console`, `css`, `html` or `yaml`. `console` is a shell
session: a line starting with `$ ` is a command (coloured as bash, its `$ ` dimmed and not
selectable) and any other line is output; with `copy` only the commands are copied, without the
`$ `. `label` names the language or file (`bash`, `css`) in a caption above the code. `text` (the
default) leaves the code in one colour, for a block that is not a language. Give the text as `children` or as `lines`. Long lines wrap, so
nothing is cut off and a command stays one copyable line; `overflow="scroll"` keeps lines whole
and scrolls them sideways under a themed scrollbar, for code whose layout matters. With
`overflow="scroll"`, a strip wider than its box is a tab stop named by `label`, else "Code". Every
other figure prop goes on the root `<figure>`. For one short line to copy, `CopyLine` is the
smaller box.

props.name: copy
props.description:
A copy button beside the code, which copies it exactly as given (a `console` block copies only
its commands). On a page rendered to static HTML without hydration, inline `copyScript` and it works there too.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: A caption above the code naming its language or file (`bash`, `theme.css`).

props.name: language
props.description: What the code is written in; `text` (the default) colours nothing.

props.name: lines
props.description: The code as one array entry per line, in place of `children`.

props.name: overflow
props.description:
What a line longer than the box does: `wrap` onto the next line (the default, nothing is cut
off), or `scroll` sideways inside the box.

CodeExample.name: CodeExample
CodeExample.description:
One framed example: the rendered `children` on top and the `code` that makes them attached
underneath, in a single bordered box with one divider between. With `copy`, a copy
button beside the code copies it exactly as given (client JS; off by default). An optional `caption` is the frame's last band. The code is React, so
it is coloured as TSX. The preview is its own height, never padded to match a neighbour, down to
a shared minimum so two frames side by side start alike. A wide preview or a long line of code
scrolls inside the frame, under a themed scrollbar, instead of widening the page or
wrapping. Inside a `Prose` the preview stays on the app scale, so a demo looks as the component
does anywhere else; the caption is outside it.

props.name: caption
props.description: One note on the example, under the code.

props.name: code
props.description: The source shown under the preview, newlines kept.

props.name: copy
props.description:
A copy button beside the code. On a page rendered to static HTML without hydration, inline
`copyScript` and it works there too.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

colourSchemeScript.name: colourSchemeScript
colourSchemeScript.description:
JavaScript to inline in `<head>`, before first paint: applies the stored scheme, else the
system one, to `<html>` as `applyColourScheme` does. Without it a light user sees a dark flash.
It then keeps following, as `followColourScheme` does: a choice made in another tab, and the system
switching while nothing is stored.

ColourSchemeToggle.name: ColourSchemeToggle
ColourSchemeToggle.description:
A sun/moon button that switches `<html>` between light and dark and remembers the choice. It shows the scheme you would switch to.
A click that lands on the system's own scheme forgets the stored choice, so the page follows the system again; a click away from it stores the choice.
With `store` on, the page also follows a choice made in another tab and, while nothing is stored, the system switching. Pair it with `colourSchemeScript` in `<head>`, unless you pass `schemes` or `defaultValue`: the script knows only the `dark` class and the stored choice, so an app that sets the scheme itself leaves it out.

An app whose light scheme has a class of its own passes `schemes` (`{ light: "my-light", dark: "dark" }`);
the toggle swaps those classes, and `schemeClass` gives the same one for the server to render on `<html>`.
An app that knows the scheme on the server (from a cookie) passes it as `defaultValue`, so the server
markup, the hydrating client and the `<html>` class agree; persist a change from `onChange`.
The icon and the button's accessible name follow the class on `<html>` through CSS (the name is
two visually hidden "Switch to …" spans, one hidden by `display:none`), so even without `defaultValue`
a dark page shows the sun and is named `lightLabel` ("Switch to light theme") from the first frame, with no
script. Only the tooltip catches up once the client has hydrated.
`store={false}` skips `localStorage`, for an app that keeps the choice in a server cookie and
writes it from `onChange`. Every other button prop (`id`, `data-*`, `aria-*`) goes on the button.

props.name: darkLabel
props.description: The button's accessible name and tooltip on a light page, where it switches to dark.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The scheme the server rendered. What the server and the hydrating client show; the real state follows right after.

props.name: lightLabel
props.description: The button's accessible name and tooltip on a dark page, where it switches to light.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Called with the new scheme after a click, for an app that persists the choice itself (a cookie).
`followsSystem` is true when the new scheme is the system's: forget the choice (clear the cookie)
rather than store it, so the page follows the system again.

props.name: schemes
props.description: The class each scheme puts on `<html>`.

props.name: size
props.description: The button's height, as an `IconButton`'s.

props.name: store
props.description: Remember the choice in `localStorage`. `false` leaves persisting to `onChange`.

ColourSwatch.name: ColourSwatch
ColourSwatch.description:
A small square in a measured colour, with its `label` and its hex `value` beside it in mono: a
colour read off a page, a screenshot or a theme. The colour is the data on show, not a look, so
it is painted from `value`; anything but a `#rrggbb` value draws an empty swatch and no value.
A hairline edges the square, so a colour close to the page still shows. The square is
decorative: the label and the value say the colour.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the colour is, as "Background" or "Accent", shown before the value.

props.name: value
props.description: The colour, as `#rrggbb`. Anything else draws an empty swatch and leaves the value out.

Combobox.name: Combobox
Combobox.description:
A text field that filters a list of choices as the person types, for a choice from more items
than a `Select` reads well (a country, a time zone, a teammate): React Aria's `ComboBox`. Typing
narrows the list by label; arrow keys move through it, Enter picks, Escape closes it. The chevron
opens the whole list. Its value is the chosen item's `value`, posted under `name`. `label`, `hint`,
`error`, `required` and `disabled` are a `DateField`'s; `size` and `width` an `Input`'s. Inside a
modal `Dialog` the list draws in the dialog. While `loading` the label is drawn and the field is a
bone of its height.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The item's `value` it starts with, uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and its button.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: The line the list shows when nothing matches what was typed, for an app in another language.

props.name: error
props.description: Marks the field invalid and shows this in red under the hint, announced politely.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the field that says more; it stays while an error shows under it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The choices, in order; typing filters them by label.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible label, above it. Without one, name the field with `aria-label`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: name
props.description: Posts the chosen item's `value` in a form under this key.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the chosen item's `value`, or `null` when the choice is cleared.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks a choice required: the field is `aria-required`, and an empty one is invalid.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is compact, `text-sm` with less padding, for dense forms and table rows; `md` is `text-base`;
`lg` is `text-lg` with more padding, for a hero form. Under an `AppShell density="compact"` each
is one type step down, and on a touch screen a field is never under 16px.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as a `Button`'s
does: give the field and the buttons in its row the same value, so the row stays aligned.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen item's `value`, controlled, with `onChange`. `null` is nothing chosen.

props.name: width
props.description: `full` (default) fills the parent; `fill` grows to fill the room left in a row beside other items (it can shrink to nothing, so buttons stay on the line); `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` are fixed; `auto` adds no width class, so the control is as wide as the browser makes it.

ConfirmDialog.name: ConfirmDialog
ConfirmDialog.description:
A `Dialog` that asks before an action: the question as its title, the consequence under it, and
Cancel beside the one action. It is an `alertdialog` and opens on Cancel, so a stray Enter cancels.
Render it only while it is open.

props.name: busyLabel
props.description: What the confirm button says while `onConfirm` runs, such as "Deleting…".

props.name: cancel
props.description: The cancel button's text, for an app in another language.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The name of the close button in the top corner, for an app in another language.

props.name: confirm
props.description: The confirm button's text, the action as a verb: "Delete".

props.name: description
props.description: The consequence, in one sentence: "This removes the build and every snapshot in it." It describes the dialog.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the dialog closes: Cancel, Esc, the backdrop, the close button, or a confirm that went through.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description:
Runs the action. A returned promise keeps the confirm button busy until it settles: resolving
closes the dialog, and a rejection shows its message in the dialog and keeps it open.

props.name: title
props.description: The question, naming the action: "Delete build?". It is the dialog's accessible name.

props.name: tone
props.description: `danger` for an action that destroys or cannot be undone, which draws the confirm button red.

Container.name: Container
Container.description:
The one content edge: every page's width and side padding. This file is the only place they are
defined, so a header, a page and a footer inside a Container start at the same x.

props.name: as
props.description: The element: `div`, `main`, `header`, `footer`, `section` or `nav`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the rendered element, for a parent that measures or scrolls it.

CopyButton.name: CopyButton
CopyButton.description: Writes `text` to the clipboard and shows `copiedLabel` for two seconds, then `label` again; a refused or missing clipboard shows `failedLabel` instead. Defaults to `type="button"` and is at least 24px square. Its accessible name stays `label`; a polite status region beside it announces `copiedLabel` or `failedLabel` on each press and empties again when the label goes back. Every other button prop, `disabled` included, goes on the `<button>`. Nothing is styled by a `<style>` element, so it works under a strict CSP. On a page rendered to static HTML without hydration, inline `copyScript` and the button works there too.

props.name: copiedLabel
props.description: The text shown for two seconds once the copy has gone through, and announced.

props.name: failedLabel
props.description:
The text shown for two seconds when the browser refuses the copy or has no clipboard, and
announced. Keep it about as long as `copiedLabel`, since the button is as wide as the longest.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's text, and its accessible name.

props.name: text
props.description: What goes on the clipboard.

CopyLine.name: CopyLine
CopyLine.description: One line of mono text in a box, with a `CopyButton`: a command or a token to paste elsewhere. `label` says what the line is, and the button is named "Copy <label>" (it still reads "Copy"), so several lines on a page can be told apart. `disabled` disables the button, e.g. until hydration. An `id`, `data-*` and `aria-*` go on the root `<div>`, so `data-testid` lands there; the `<code>` holds only `text`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the copy button, e.g. until hydration.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the line is, in a few lower-case words ("install command", "API token"): the copy button's accessible name is "Copy " and this.

props.name: text
props.description: The line shown, and what the button copies.

copyScript.name: copyScript
copyScript.description:
JavaScript to inline once on a page that is rendered to static HTML and never hydrated, so every
`CopyButton` (and the `CopyLine`, `CodeBlock` and `CodeExample` copy buttons) works there too.
One click listener on `document` reads what to copy from the button's `data-copy-text`, writes the
clipboard, then does what `CopyButton` does: cancels a run in progress, holds the copied (or, on a
refused or missing clipboard, the failed) label in view for two seconds with two Web Animations,
and puts a new node holding that label in the status region beside the button, so a screen reader
hears each press; the run's end empties the region. No timer and no stylesheet. Whichever of the
script and a hydrated button's own handler hears a click first copies and flags the event
(`copyHandled`), and the other skips it: one copy per click.

DateField.name: DateField
DateField.description:
A segmented date input, in the order of its `locale` (by default the browser's): DD / MM / YYYY
in en-GB. Values are `CalendarDate`s; `name` posts it as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `calendar` adds a calendar button that opens a month view in a popover, at the
same height as the plain field; `defaultOpen` opens it on mount. While `loading` the label is
drawn and the field is a bone of its height.

props.name: calendar
props.description: Adds a calendar button that opens a month view in a popover; the field is a date picker.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The calendar's footer button that empties the field, for an app in another language. Only a `calendar` field takes `clearLabel`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open the calendar on mount. Only a `calendar` field takes `defaultOpen`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The date it starts with, uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field: no typing, no calendar.

props.name: error
props.description:
Marks the field invalid and shows this in red under the hint, announced politely, in place of
the built-in message (an impossible date, or one outside min/max). Like `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the field that says more; it stays while an error shows under it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible label, above it. Without one, name the field with `aria-label`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: locale
props.description:
The locale the field writes its date in, a BCP 47 tag: `en-GB` is DD/MM/YYYY, `en-US`
MM/DD/YYYY, `en-ZA` YYYY/MM/DD. It sets the order of the segments, the month names, the
calendar's first weekday and the dates in its messages. Without it the field follows the app's
own `I18nProvider`, or else the browser's language.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The latest date allowed: a later one marks the field invalid with its own message.

props.name: minValue
props.description: The earliest date allowed: an earlier one marks the field invalid with its own message.

props.name: monthLabel
props.description: The month dropdown's name, for an app in another language. Only a `calendar` field takes `monthLabel`.

props.name: name
props.description: Posts the date in a form as `YYYY-MM-DD` under this key, or an empty string, whatever the `locale`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new date, or `null` when the field is cleared or the date is incomplete.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks a date required: the field is `aria-required`, and an empty one is invalid.

props.name: size
props.description:
The field's height and text, on the same scale as an `Input`: `sm` is `text-sm`, `md` `text-base`,
`lg` `text-lg`, one step down under an `AppShell density="compact"`, and never under 16px on touch.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as an `Input`'s does.

props.name: value
props.description: The date shown, controlled, with `onChange`; `null` is an empty field.

props.name: yearLabel
props.description: The year dropdown's name, for an app in another language. Only a `calendar` field takes `yearLabel`.

DateRangePicker.name: DateRangePicker
DateRangePicker.description:
A from and to date in one field, each side in the locale's order, and a calendar button that opens one
Monday-first month, where two presses pick the range. `presets` adds the app's ready-made ranges
above the month. The range is reported only when both sides are complete, real dates within
min/max and the start is on or before the end; otherwise `null`.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The calendar's footer button that empties the range.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open the calendar on mount.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The range shown first when the picker holds its own value.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field: no typing, no calendar.

props.name: endLabel
props.description: The name of the end date's segments, for a screen reader.

props.name: endName
props.description: Posts the end as `YYYY-MM-DD` in a form, or `""` while there is no range.

props.name: error
props.description:
Marks the field invalid and shows this in red under the hint, announced politely, in place of
the built-in message (an impossible date, or one outside min/max). Like `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the field that says more; it stays while an error shows under it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible label, above it. Without one, name the field with `aria-label`.

props.name: locale
props.description:
The locale the field writes its date in, a BCP 47 tag: `en-GB` is DD/MM/YYYY, `en-US`
MM/DD/YYYY, `en-ZA` YYYY/MM/DD. It sets the order of the segments, the month names, the
calendar's first weekday and the dates in its messages. Without it the field follows the app's
own `I18nProvider`, or else the browser's language.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The latest date allowed: a later one marks the field invalid with its own message.

props.name: minValue
props.description: The earliest date allowed: an earlier one marks the field invalid with its own message.

props.name: monthLabel
props.description: The month dropdown's name, for an app in another language.

props.name: onChange
props.type: ((range: { start: CalendarDate; end: CalendarDate } | null) => void)
props.description: Called with the range once both sides make one, and with `null` when they stop making one.

props.name: presets
props.description:
Ready-made ranges, a row of buttons above the month. The app builds them from its own today;
the picker has none of its own and never reads the clock.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks a date required: the field is `aria-required`, and an empty one is invalid.

props.name: size
props.description:
The field's height and text, on the same scale as an `Input`: `sm` is `text-sm`, `md` `text-base`,
`lg` `text-lg`, one step down under an `AppShell density="compact"`, and never under 16px on touch.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as an `Input`'s does.

props.name: startLabel
props.description: The name of the start date's segments, for a screen reader.

props.name: startName
props.description: Posts the start as `YYYY-MM-DD` in a form, or `""` while there is no range.

props.name: toLabel
props.description: The word between the two dates.

props.name: value
props.description: The range, or `null` for none. Reported only when both days are complete, real and in order.

props.name: yearLabel
props.description: The year dropdown's name, for an app in another language.

DateTimeField.name: DateTimeField
DateTimeField.description:
A segmented date and time input, to the minute: the date in the order of its `locale` (by default
the browser's), then hours and minutes on the clock the locale uses, 24-hour in en-GB and with
AM/PM in en-US. Values are `CalendarDateTime`s; `name` posts it as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`. It has no
calendar. While `loading` the label is drawn and the field is a bone of its height.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The date and time shown first when the field holds its own value.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field: no typing, no calendar.

props.name: error
props.description:
Marks the field invalid and shows this in red under the hint, announced politely, in place of
the built-in message (an impossible date, or one outside min/max). Like `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the field that says more; it stays while an error shows under it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible label, above it. Without one, name the field with `aria-label`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: locale
props.description:
The locale the field writes its date in, a BCP 47 tag: `en-GB` is DD/MM/YYYY, `en-US`
MM/DD/YYYY, `en-ZA` YYYY/MM/DD. It sets the order of the segments, the month names, the
calendar's first weekday and the dates in its messages. Without it the field follows the app's
own `I18nProvider`, or else the browser's language.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The latest date and time the field takes; later ones are invalid.

props.name: minValue
props.description: The earliest date and time the field takes; earlier ones are invalid.

props.name: name
props.description:
Posts the date and time in a form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` (24-hour) under this key, or an empty
string, whatever the `locale`.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Called with the date and time once every segment is filled, the day exists and it is within
`minValue`/`maxValue`, and with `null` when it stops being one.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks a date required: the field is `aria-required`, and an empty one is invalid.

props.name: size
props.description:
The field's height and text, on the same scale as an `Input`: `sm` is `text-sm`, `md` `text-base`,
`lg` `text-lg`, one step down under an `AppShell density="compact"`, and never under 16px on touch.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as an `Input`'s does.

props.name: value
props.description: The date and time shown, controlled, with `onChange`; `null` is an empty field.

DetailLayout.name: DetailLayout
DetailLayout.description:
A detail page: header, then `children` (two thirds from `lg`) beside `aside` (one third), which
stacks below on a smaller screen: a `SideColumn asideWidth="third"` under a `PageHeader`. `sticky` keeps the aside in view from `lg` as a long page
scrolls: it sticks under AppShell's header and, if it is taller than the room left, scrolls
itself so its end stays reachable. While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right of the title on `sm` and up, below it on a phone.

props.name: aside
props.description: The side column: one third from `lg`, below `children` on a smaller screen.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: Names the aside's landmark (`aria-label`), so a page with another complementary landmark can tell them apart. It does not fold the aside. Left out, the aside is unnamed.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
From `lg`, keeps the aside in view under the header as the page scrolls; an aside taller than
the screen scrolls inside itself. Off by default, since an aside of ordinary cards may be
taller than the screen. Below `lg` the aside stacks as ever.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

Dialog.name: Dialog
Dialog.description:
A modal on the browser's own `<dialog>`: it is opened with `showModal()` on mount, so render it
only while it is open. The page behind goes inert, Esc closes it and focus stays inside; a click
on the backdrop (the `<dialog>` element itself, not its contents) closes it too, and so does the
close button in its top corner, which every dialog has. The close button comes last in the
keyboard order, so the open focuses the first field, not it. A windowed dialog is never taller
than the screen: a tall body scrolls and the title and footer stay on screen, and a scroll inside
it never carries on to the page behind.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The name of the close button in the top corner, for an app in another language.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted line under the title.

props.name: error
props.description:
What went wrong with the whole submit (the server refused it, no connection): a danger
`Callout`, announced as an alert, between the body and the footer, so it stays beside the
buttons however tall the body is. An error about one field is that `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions under the body, right-aligned: Cancel (`variant="ghost"`), then the one main action.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onClose
props.description:
Called when the dialog closes: its close button, Esc, a click on the backdrop, or a
`<form method="dialog">` submit.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description:
Makes the dialog a form: one `<form noValidate>` holds the body, the `error` and the footer,
so a `Button type="submit"` in the footer or Enter in a field submits it, with no `form`
