attribute or id. The default is prevented before this runs, and a rejection is yours to
catch and show as `error`. Once the submit settles, the focus moves to the first field marked
invalid (`aria-invalid="true"`), if any. Put no `<form method="dialog">` in the footer of a form dialog:
it would nest a form.

props.name: title
props.description: The dialog's accessible name, shown as its heading.

props.name: width
props.description:
The panel's width: `sm` (320px) is a list, `md` (440px) holds a form, `lg` (640px) a wider
form or a table. `full` fills the whole screen, for media or a player: the body takes the
height between the header and the footer and scrolls if it is taller. It has no backdrop to
click: its close button and Esc close it.

A single photo or video is a `Lightbox`.

Disclosure.name: Disclosure
Disclosure.description:
A summary line with a chevron over a body that opens and closes under it. The summary is a
button with `aria-expanded`, and Enter and Space toggle it; the body is hidden while closed.
It starts closed and keeps its own state; `defaultOpen` starts it open. To drive it from the
app, pass `open` with `onOpenChange`.

`bordered` draws it as a panel: a bordered box with the summary as a roomy row across the top
(the hover fill of a `ListRow`) and the body padded under a hairline, for a section that opens in
place in a page of cards. Plain, it is a line of text with the body indented under it.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Draws it as a bordered panel: the summary a full-width row, the body padded under a hairline.

props.name: children
props.description: The body, shown while open.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Starts with the body showing.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the summary is pressed.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the body shows, for an app that holds the state; pass `onOpenChange` with it.

props.name: summary
props.description: The always-visible line: the button that toggles the body.

Display.name: Display
Display.description:
Marketing-scale headline: the one line at the top of a public page. `h1`,
text-4xl/tight semibold, primary text, growing to text-6xl on wider screens.
`PageHeading` is the title of an ordinary page, a step below; a brochure hero needs a display
scale, so it gets its own pinned role rather than callers overriding PageHeading's size.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; each role has a semantic default.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Divider.name: Divider
Divider.description: A hairline rule in the theme's line colour: between a heading and its content, or above a footer. Space around it is the layout's.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

DocsLayout.name: DocsLayout
DocsLayout.description:
A docs page: a `SidebarLayout` whose rail is the docs `nav` (each group's title over its links,
folded behind a disclosure named `asideLabel` below `md`), and a canvas of the page's title, an
"On this page" list of its `contents`, the article and the previous and next links.

The contents list is rendered once: from `xl` a 12rem column right of the article that sticks
under the header, below `xl` a closed disclosure above the article. `current` marks the heading
being read; it is a value the page passes (a site that follows the reader computes it), with no
scroll spy inside. The previous and next links are links, not cards, so they add no heading to
the page's outline.

While `loading` the canvas waits, as in `SidebarLayout`: an empty title is a bone and what the
article holds draws its own bones; the nav, the contents list and the previous and next links are
navigation, drawn as themselves. The layout owns the wait.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description:
Names the rail's landmark, and the disclosure it folds behind below `md` ("Docs", "All
components"), as `SidebarLayout`'s `asideLabel` does.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: children
props.description: The article. Wrap long text in a `Prose`.

props.name: contents
props.description: The page's own headings, in order. With fewer than two there is no "On this page" list.

props.name: contentsLabel
props.description: The contents list's name and its label.

props.name: current
props.description: The id of the heading being read: its entry is marked (`aria-current="location"`). A value the page passes, never tracked inside.

props.name: description
props.description: The line under the title (a `Lead`).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: nav
props.description: The docs nav, in reading order: each group's title over a vertical pill list of its pages.

props.name: next
props.description: The page after this one in reading order.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The word over the next page's label.

props.name: previous
props.description: The page before this one in reading order.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The word over the previous page's label.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's title, its `h1`.

Drawer.name: Drawer
Drawer.description:
A modal slide-over anchored to the right edge, on the browser's own `<dialog>`: it is opened
with `showModal()` on mount, so render it only while it is open. The page behind goes inert, Esc
closes it and focus stays inside; a click on the scrim (the `<dialog>` element itself, not its
contents) closes it too, and on touch a swipe to the right drags it off (a short one springs
back). The header holds the title, an optional `description` under it and a close button; the
body scrolls between it and an optional pinned `footer`, and a scroll in it never carries on to
the page behind. `onSubmit` makes it a form and `error` shows what went wrong with the submit, as
on a `Dialog`.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the close button.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted line under the title, as on a `Dialog`.

props.name: error
props.description:
What went wrong with the whole submit, as on a `Dialog`: a danger `Callout`, announced as an
alert, pinned between the body and the footer. An error about one field is that `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions pinned under the scrolling body, right-aligned: Cancel (`variant="ghost"`), then the one main action.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the drawer closes: Esc, a click on the scrim, the close button or a swipe to the right on touch.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description:
Makes the drawer a form, as on a `Dialog`: one `<form noValidate>` holds the body, the `error`
and the footer, so a `Button type="submit"` in the footer or Enter in a field submits it. The
default is prevented before this runs, and a rejection is yours to catch and show as `error`.
Once the submit settles, the focus moves to the first field marked invalid
(`aria-invalid="true"`), if any.

props.name: title
props.description: The drawer's accessible name, shown as its heading.

props.name: width
props.description: The panel's width: `md` holds a form or a record; `sm` (320px) is narrower and `lg` (640px) wider.

EmbedFrame.name: EmbedFrame
EmbedFrame.description:
A rounded, clipped frame with a hairline, at a fixed height, for a map or an `<iframe>`: the
embed in `children` fills it. `status` lays a centred overlay over the embed while it loads or
after it failed; the embed stays mounted under it, so it can finish loading. The frame is a
region named by `label`.

props.name: children
props.description: The embed: an `<iframe>` or a map's container. It fills the frame.

props.name: errorLabel
props.description: The words over the embed when `status` is `error`: say what failed and what to do.

props.name: height
props.description:
`sm` 18rem, `md` 24rem, or `viewport`, 55% of the small viewport's height, for a map that is
the page's main content.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the frame's region: what the embed shows, as "Map of the shops".

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while `status` is `loading`.

props.name: status
props.description:
`loading` lays a pulsing cover over the embed and marks the region busy; `error` lays
`errorLabel` over it, announced. Set it from the embed's own load and error events.

EmptyState.name: EmptyState
EmptyState.description:
The one empty look: what a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet. Give it
to the part's `empty` slot (`ListLayout`, `CardGrid`, `TableBody`, `Timeline`, `ChatThread`, a
`Stack as="ul"`), which shows it when the part has no children and picks its size.

`md` is a centred `title`, the `children` as the explanation under it (a `Text`, then `Steps` for
a "get started" list), and `actions` (buttons, links) in a centred row at the bottom, with an
optional `icon` above the title. A named `<section>`. On its own it draws a dashed frame round
itself; inside a `Card` the card is the frame. `level` is the title's heading level, one below
the heading that holds it: a 2 on the page, a 3 in a `Section`.

`sm` is the one-line form for inside a table, a timeline or a list: the title as one centred
muted line, the `children` under it in the same small text and the `actions` after. It is a plain
block with no heading and no landmark, so a table cell or a card does not grow a region.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons or links in a centred row at the bottom.

props.name: icon
props.description: One of the library's icons, at feature size in the muted ink above the title.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: level
props.default: one below the heading that holds it: 2 on the page
props.description: The title's heading level, 2 to 6. It does not change how the title looks.

props.name: padding
props.description:
`inset` pads all four sides, for an empty state in a `Card flush`, whose body has no padding
of its own. `default` pads above and below only. On its own, outside a card, it pads all four
sides inside its frame either way.

props.name: size
props.default: the slot's: sm in a TableBody, a Timeline or a Stack as="ul", else md
props.description:
`md` is the titled block; `sm` one muted line with no heading, for inside a table, a timeline or
a list. `icon` and `level` do nothing at `sm`.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, centred: what is missing ("No projects yet"). It names the section.

ErrorPage.name: ErrorPage
ErrorPage.description:
500 or any failure. `detail` is the error text, shown in a `CodeBlock` under the copy; pass it
only where a reader may see it (a request id, a message), never a stack trace. `onRetry` adds a
"Try again" button, unless `actions` replaces it.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to add a button; `homeLabel` and `retryLabel` only reword the built-in ones.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: detail
props.description: The error text, in a `CodeBlock` under the copy: a request id or a message a reader may see, never a stack trace.

props.name: detailLabel
props.description: The name of the `detail` block, for an app in another language.

props.name: homeLabel
props.description: The button to the `LinkProvider`'s `home`, for an app in another language.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Adds a "Try again" button that calls it, unless `actions` replaces the button.

props.name: retryLabel
props.description: The button `onRetry` adds, for an app in another language.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

Field.name: Field
Field.description:
A label above a control, with a hint line under it and, when set, an error line under the hint
(an alert icon and red text, announced politely). The hint stays while the error shows.
`required` marks the label with a red asterisk and makes the control inside `required`.
Inside a `FormGrid`, `span="full"` runs the field across both columns. The `Input`, `Select`,
`Textarea` or `FileDrop` inside takes the label, the note (`aria-describedby`) and, with an error,
`aria-invalid` and a red edge by itself: give it no `id` and the Field no `htmlFor`. While
`loading` the label is drawn and the control is a bone of its height, read from the density
around it (`sm` in a `sm` card or table).

props.name: error
props.description: A red line under the hint, with an alert icon; the control is `aria-invalid` while it shows.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the control that says more.

props.name: htmlFor
props.description: A fixed id for the control inside, only when something else must name it. Unset, the Field makes one.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The text above the control.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description:
Keeps the `label` in the page for assistive tech and draws no text, for a control whose purpose
is plain from what surrounds it (a search box in a toolbar). `label` stays required, so the
control always has a name. With `layout="row"` the field draws as a column: an empty label
column helps nobody.

props.name: layout
props.description:
`row` puts the label beside the control, for a compact setting or a drawer row; the hint or
error sits under the control. Every row label takes the same fixed column, so stacked rows line
their controls up; a long label wraps inside it. `column` puts the label above it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: required
props.description:
The control must be filled: a red asterisk after the label (hidden from assistive tech) and
`required` on the `Input`, `Select`, `Textarea` or `FileDrop` inside.

props.name: span
props.description: `full` spans every column of a `FormGrid`; unset takes one. It does nothing outside a `FormGrid`.

FieldDialog.name: FieldDialog
FieldDialog.description: A `Dialog` with one text field and Cancel / submit buttons. Render it only while open.

props.name: busyLabel
props.description: What the submit button says while `onSubmit` runs.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: The button that closes the dialog without submitting, for an app in another language.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted line under the title.

props.name: emptyReason
props.description: The field's error when it is submitted empty: the submit button stays enabled, so this says what is missing.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the field.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The visible label above the field, which names it.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the dialog closes: Cancel, Esc, the backdrop, or a resolved `onSubmit`.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Gets the trimmed value. Resolving closes the dialog; a rejection shows its message in it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder.

props.name: submit
props.description: The submit button's text.

props.name: title
props.description: The dialog's heading and accessible name.

Fieldset.name: Fieldset
Fieldset.description:
A labelled group of controls: several `Checkbox`es answering one question, a set of `Field`s that
belong together, or the filter chips of one facet (a `ButtonGroup` of `outline` `sm` pressed
`Button`s). It is a `<fieldset>` named by its `label`, drawn as its `<legend>` in the `Field`
label's look, over the children in one column; a `ButtonGroup` or a `FormGrid` inside lays out a
row. `hint` is a muted line under the group and its `aria-describedby`; `error` adds a red line
under it with an alert icon, announced politely. `disabled` disables every control inside. One choice of several is a
`RadioGroup`, never inside a `Fieldset`. Other props go on the `<fieldset>`.

props.name: children
props.description: `Checkbox`es, `Field`s (in a `FormGrid` for a row), or a `ButtonGroup` of chips.

props.name: error
props.description: A red line under the hint, with an alert icon, announced politely.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the group.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's name, drawn as its `<legend>`.

FileDrop.name: FileDrop
FileDrop.description:
A dashed drop zone around a file input. The input covers the whole zone, invisible, so a click
opens the file dialog and a file dragged onto it is taken by the browser as it is by any file
input. `children` is the prompt; show the chosen file's name there from `onChange`. The label also shows
the keyboard focus ring, the input being invisible. Every prop (`accept`, `multiple`, `name`, `disabled`, `onChange`) goes on the input.

props.name: accept
props.description: The file types it takes, as on `<input type="file">`: `"image/*"`, `".pdf"`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the drop zone; say why in its `Field` hint.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Takes several files at once.

props.name: name
props.description: The key the files post under in a form.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` is a compact chip or tile: dense padding; `lg` is one step roomier than `md`.

FlowDiagram.name: FlowDiagram
FlowDiagram.description:
Boxes joined by arrows, laid out for you: a flow, a pipeline, a state machine. Give it the
`nodes` and the `edges` between them and it places every box in ranks `direction` (`down` or
`right`) and routes every arrow round them, loops and arrows back up included (dagre's layered
layout). Each box is as wide as its label and its `content`, so no text spills; boxes with a
`group` share a dashed frame; `active` rings one box in the accent.

The diagram is drawn at its own size and scrolls inside its own box when it is wider or taller
than the room it has, so it never makes the page scroll sideways. It is an image named by
`label`; every box and every arrow is also a visually hidden list after it.

`overlay` draws on top of the diagram in its own coordinates: it is handed the laid-out
`FlowLayout` (each box's place and each arrow's SVG path), for a marker that follows an arrow.
It is not hit by the pointer, and it is hidden from a screen reader.

While `loading` with no nodes it draws one bone the height of a small diagram.

props.name: active
props.description: The `id` of the one box to ring in the accent: the current step, the state a thing is in now.

props.name: direction
props.description: Where the arrows run: `down` (top to bottom) or `right` (start to end).

props.name: edges
props.description: The arrows. One whose `from` or `to` is not a node's `id` is not drawn.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the diagram shows: its accessible name, and the name of its hidden list.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: nodes
props.description: The boxes, each with a unique `id`. Their order is only a hint: the layout ranks them by the arrows.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Draws on top of the diagram, in its coordinates, from the laid-out boxes and arrow paths.

Forbidden.name: Forbidden
Forbidden.description:
403: signed in, or not, but not allowed here. The page for a route that exists and the reader may
not see; a route that is not there is a `NotFound`.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to add a button; `homeLabel` and `retryLabel` only reword the built-in ones.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: homeLabel
props.description: The button to the `LinkProvider`'s `home`, for an app in another language.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

FormGrid.name: FormGrid
FormGrid.description:
Two columns of `Field`s once the grid is 36rem wide, one below that. It folds by its own width,
not the viewport's, so it stays one column in a `Dialog` or a side column. A `Field` takes one
column; `span="full"` runs it across both, and a `FormRow` is always full width.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

FormLayout.name: FormLayout
FormLayout.description: A form page: header (no header `actions`), then a `max-w-3xl` column that starts at the Container's start edge (it is not re-centred), with an `actions` row at the end. `note` is a muted line under that row, set apart from the form: a closing remark about the whole submit (when you will hear back, what happens next), never a field's hint. `error` is the submit's failure, a danger `Callout` (an alert) directly above that row. Other props go on the `<form>`. While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too.

props.name: actions
props.description: The row at the end of the form: its submit and cancel buttons.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: error
props.description:
What went wrong with the whole submit (the server refused it, no connection), announced as an
alert directly above the `actions`. An error about one field is that `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: note
props.description:
A muted line under the `actions`, set apart from them: a closing remark about the whole form
("We reply within two working days."). A note about one field is that `Field`'s `hint`.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

FormRow.name: FormRow
FormRow.description:
An inline-edit row: several controls side by side with proportional widths (`FormRowField`
`span` 1 to 4), optional `actions` after them (a save button), and one `hint` or `error` line
under the whole row. Every control sits on the bottom edge, so the actions line up with them
whatever the labels do. Narrower than 36rem (the row's own width, not the viewport's) the fields
and the actions stack.

The row owns the note, so the fields beside each other keep their height: a `FormRowField` has
no `hint` or `error` of its own.

props.name: actions
props.description: A button or two after the last field. It keeps its own width.

props.name: error
props.description: A red line under the hint, announced politely, as `Field`'s is.

props.name: hint
props.description: One muted line under the whole row.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

FormRowField.name: FormRowField
FormRowField.description:
A compact label over one control, for a `FormRow`. `span` is its share of the row (1 default).
While `loading` the label is drawn and the control is a bone of its height, as in a `Field`.

props.name: htmlFor
props.description: The id of the control inside; the label's htmlFor.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The small label above the control.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: span
props.description: The field's share of the row, 1 to 4: a `span` of 2 is twice as wide as a 1.

fromISODate.name: fromISODate
fromISODate.description: The `CalendarDate` of a `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string; `null` for an empty, malformed or impossible one.
fromISODate.signature: fromISODate(iso: string | null | undefined): CalendarDate | null

fromISODateTime.name: fromISODateTime
fromISODateTime.description:
The `CalendarDateTime` of a `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` string; `null` for an empty, malformed or
impossible one (a day the month does not have, an hour past 23).
fromISODateTime.signature: fromISODateTime(iso: string | null | undefined): CalendarDateTime | null

fromXState.name: fromXState
fromXState.description:
Turns an xstate v5 machine (the machine, or its config) into a `StateMachine` definition: one
state per top-level state node, one transition per target in each node's `on`.

- A state's `label` is its `meta.label`, else its key; its `owner` is `meta.owner`; its `kind`
  is `meta.kind` when that is one of the five, else `terminal` for a `type: "final"` node,
  `initial` for the machine's `initial`, and `normal` for the rest.
- Each `on` event, `always`, each `after` delay and each `invoke`'s `onDone` and `onError` is a
  transition. Its `event` is its `meta.label`, else the event's name (`always`, `after 500`,
  `done`, `error`). A transition with no target
  (it stays where it is), one that stays inside its own state, or one whose target is not a
  top-level state is left out.
- `state` adjusts each state, for a machine whose meta says it another way: return the state to
  draw, given its key, its config and the state the rules above made of it.

Only the top level is read: a nested state is drawn as its parent.
fromXState.signature: fromXState(machine: XStateMachineLike, options?: { state?: ((input: XStateStateInput) => StateMachineState) | undefined; }): StateMachineDefinition

FullBleedLayout.name: FullBleedLayout
FullBleedLayout.description:
Edge-to-edge `children` with an optional `aside` at the end (`lg:w-72`) that stacks below on a smaller
screen. Render it in `<AppShell bleed>`. It deliberately breaks the shared start edge: a viewer
that needs the whole width has no Container of its own, so `children` start at the viewport's
start edge. `padded` gives them the Container's padding instead (`px-4`, `sm:px-6`, `py-8`), for
a page of ordinary content beside a full-height `aside`. A `bar` is a `StickyBar` above both: the
full width, on the surface with a bottom line, sticking under AppShell's header as the page scrolls.
While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too.

props.name: aside
props.description: A side column on the right (`lg:w-72`) on a tinted surface; below `lg` it stacks under `children`.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: Names the `<aside>` landmark (`aria-label`). Left out, it is unnamed.

props.name: bar
props.description: A full-width row above `children` and `aside` that sticks under the header, e.g. a viewer's title and actions. `padded` does not pad it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: padded
props.description:
Pads `children` as the Container pads every other page. Off, they run to the viewport's edges.
A notice in the column is a plain `Callout` in a `Stack`, never a `Callout banner`.

Hero.name: Hero
Hero.description:
A landing page's top block: an overline, the display title (the page's `h1`) and the lede under
it, over a soft glow of three tilted ribbons that drift slowly behind the text. The glow is always
there and its colours and strength are the theme's (the palette's `glow` role), so a paper theme
keeps it faint. It is anchored to the text's own column (`max-w-3xl`, at the parent's start edge,
or in its middle with `align="center"`), never the viewport, and clipped to it, so nothing scrolls
sideways on a phone. It is `aria-hidden`, and the text sits above it. `media` puts a picture
beside the words from `md` up. A small checkbox in the top corner holds the drift still, since it
never ends on its own; under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the glow stands still and the
checkbox is not drawn. Pure markup and one inline stylesheet: it works rendered on the server with
no script. One per page, on a landing page; every other page opens with a `PageHeader`.

props.name: align
props.description:
`center` sets the words in the middle of the page, under a centred glow: a landing page
with no picture whose actions are one or two buttons. Pass the actions' `Cluster`
`justify="center"` too.

props.name: children
props.description: What follows the title: a `Lead`, and the page's first actions if it has any.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: media
props.description:
A picture beside the words from `md` up, and under them on a phone: an `Image` of the
product, at `width="full"`. The words keep the glow; the picture sits clear of it.

props.name: overline
props.description: The small label above the title, set in the monospace face.

props.name: pauseLabel
props.description: The name of the control that holds the glow still, for an app in another language.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`, at display size.

Icon.name: Icon
Icon.description:
One inline icon, sized to a fixed box (sm 14px, md 16px, lg 20px, `feature` 32px) and drawn in
`currentColor`, so it takes the text colour around it unless a `tone` says otherwise. `name`
picks one of the library's own icons, all drawn on one grid with one stroke: feature ideas
(`diff`, `baseline`, `review`, `ci`, `self-host`, `privacy`, `capture`, `branch`, `theme`,
`speed`, `search`) and UI glyphs (`chevron-right`, `chevron-down`, `close`, `external-link`,
`settings`, `bell`, `check`, `alert`, `plus`, `more`) and the ideas the docs sections stand for (`grid`, `window`,
`type`, `card`, `pointer`, `field`, `table`, `compass`, `page`, `briefcase`);
without a name, a bare `<svg>` child fills the box. It is decorative (`aria-hidden`) by
default; a `label` makes it an image with that name, for an icon that carries meaning no text
beside it says.

props.name: children
props.description: The `<svg>`, drawn in `currentColor`; it fills the box.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the icon (`role="img"`). Without one the icon is hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: name
props.description: One of the library's icons, named for the idea it stands for.

props.name: size
props.description: The box: sm 14px, md 16px (the default), lg 20px, `feature` 32px for an icon that stands for an idea on its own (a feature card). `{ base, md }` (sm, md, lg) changes at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), as the icon in a Button of that size does.

props.name: tone
props.description: A text tone. Left out, the icon takes the colour of the text around it.

IconButton.name: IconButton
IconButton.description:
A square button holding one icon from the `Icon` set (`icon`). `label` is its accessible name
and tooltip. `variant="ghost"` drops the border for a quiet action in a row or a toolbar; `size`
matches the height of a `Button` of the same size (`sm` 26px, `md` 38px, `lg` 46px; a
responsive `{ base, md }` changes at 48rem) and with no
`size` it takes its container's; `tone="danger"` is red, for delete and clear; `count` pins a
red count to the corner; `disabledReason` blocks it and shows why. Defaults to `type="button"`. `href` makes it a link instead (the app's
router link through `LinkProvider` for an in-app path, else a plain `<a>`; `external` opens a
new tab), with the same look.

props.name: count
props.description: A red count on the top corner at the end edge, for unread alerts. Not shown at 0; the name carries it for a screen reader, "Alerts, 3".

props.name: disabledReason
props.description:
Why the button cannot be pressed: it dims and is blocked (`aria-disabled`; a click, Enter and
Space do nothing) while it stays in the tab order, and the reason is its tooltip on hover,
keyboard focus and a tap, read out as its description. The name stays `label`.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the button a link to this URL; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: icon
props.description: The one icon it holds, from the `Icon` set, at the button's size.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's accessible name and its tooltip, shown on hover and on keyboard focus.

props.name: size
props.description:
The button's height, matching a `Button` or `Input` of the same size. Left out, it takes the
size of the `Card`, `ListRow` or `Table` it sits in, else `md`. `{ base: "md", md: "lg" }`
changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS.

Give it the same value as a responsive `Button` beside it.

props.name: tone
props.description: `danger` is red, for delete and clear.

props.name: variant
props.description: `outline` has a border; `ghost` has none, until the hover fill.

Image.name: Image
Image.description:
A picture in a fixed shape: `aspect` reserves the space before it loads, so the page does not
jump, and `fit` crops it to the shape or shows all of it. The corners are rounded and the frame
has a hairline. If the picture is missing or fails to load, a same-sized placeholder with a
picture mark stands in, still named by `alt`. `mat` sets it on a padded mat: `white` for a code
or a logo, `page` for a screenshot. `href` links it to its full size in a new tab. It loads
lazily unless it is the `priority` picture. A user's photo is an `Avatar`; a clickable
thumbnail with a label is a `MediaTile`. While `loading` with no `src` yet it is a bone of the same
shape, not the placeholder, which means there is no picture.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the picture shows. An empty string marks it as decoration, hidden from a screen reader.

props.name: aspect
crop
props.description:
Where `fit="cover"` crops from: `center` keeps the middle of the picture, `top` keeps its top
edge, for a screenshot whose header is the part to see.

props.name: fit
props.description:
`cover` fills the shape and crops what overflows; `contain` shows the whole picture, with the
rest of the shape left empty (a QR code, a logo).

props.name: href
props.description:
Makes the picture a link to its full size, opened in a new tab (`target="_blank"`,
`rel="noreferrer"`), named by `alt`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mat
props.description:
Sets the picture on a padded mat and shows the whole of it, as `fit="contain"`, whatever `fit`
says. `white` is white in every theme, dark ones included, so a QR code, a barcode or a logo
reads off a dark page. `page` is a ground a step below the page in each theme, for a
screenshot. Left out, there is no mat.

props.name: priority
props.description:
Marks the picture that is the page's largest one in the first view (its LCP): it loads at once
with a high fetch priority. Every other picture loads lazily, when it nears the viewport.

props.name: src
props.description:
The picture, a local path or a data URL. It is never loaded for you: this is the app's own
image. Left out, or if it fails to load, the picture is replaced by a placeholder.

props.name: width
props.description:
`sm` 96px, `md` 160px, `lg` 256px and `xl` 448px set the width, capped at the parent's; `full`
fills the parent.

InlineEdit.name: InlineEdit
InlineEdit.description:
A value that opens an editor in place, as a part inside a `TableCell` that holds more than the
value (an edit trigger in a column cell with other content, say). It shows `children` as a button with a dotted underline; a click, Enter
or Space swaps it for `renderEditor(close)` and moves the focus into the editor. The part keeps
its own open state. The editor calls `close` when it has saved, and Esc closes it: both put the
focus back on the value. A press outside it or Tab out of it closes it too and leaves the focus
where it went, so the editor saves its value on its own change or submit, never on a close. Put
the control in the part itself, not in a popover of its own, which counts as outside. It takes
the alignment of the cell around it. It is a block that bleeds half a rem into the padding of
the cell it sits in, so it belongs inside a `TableCell`; a cell that holds only the value is a
`TableEditCell`. `data-*` and `aria-*` go on the button, and on the editor's group while open.

props.name: children
props.description: The value, shown while closed.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button does, for a screen reader, heard after the value: "Edit category". It also names the editor.

props.name: renderEditor
props.description: The control that edits the value, drawn while open. `close` shuts it and returns the focus to the value.

Input.name: Input
Input.description:
A text input. `icon` names a leading icon inside the field (`icon="search"`). `prefix` puts
short text inside the border before the value, such as a currency symbol; it is for a plain
field, not with an `icon` or `type="search"`. `numeric` is a field for a figure: an amount
(`<Input prefix="R" numeric />`) or a count (`numeric inputMode="numeric"`). It right-aligns the
value in tabular figures and brings up the phone's number keypad (`inputMode="decimal"` unless
you pass your own), and stays a text field, so "1 250" is kept as typed; never use
`type="number"` for a figure a person types. `type="search"` drops the browser's own search look and shows a clear button at the
trailing edge while the field has a value, named by `clearLabel`, and Escape clears it. The `ref` reaches the `<input>`.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The name of a `type="search"` field's clear button, for an app in another language.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field; say why in its `Field` hint.

props.name: icon
props.description: A leading icon inside the field, by name (`search`). Not with `prefix`.

props.name: name
props.description: The key the value posts under in a form.

props.name: numeric
props.description:
A field for a figure (an amount, a count): the value right-aligned in tabular figures, and
`inputMode="decimal"` unless you pass your own (`numeric` for a whole number). It stays a
text field, so the value is kept as typed; parsing it is yours. Ignored on `type="search"`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: A hint shown while the field is empty; never the label.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short text inside the border before the value (a currency symbol). For a plain field: not with `icon` or `type="search"`.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<input>` itself, for focus control.

props.name: required
props.description: The form will not submit while the field is empty.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is compact, `text-sm` with less padding, for dense forms and table rows; `md` is `text-base`;
`lg` is `text-lg` with more padding, for a hero form. Under an `AppShell density="compact"` each
is one type step down, and on a touch screen a field is never under 16px.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as a `Button`'s
does: give the field and the buttons in its row the same value, so the row stays aligned.

props.name: type
props.description: The kind of value: `"text"`, `"email"`, `"search"`, `"password"` and the rest.

props.name: width
props.description: `full` (default) fills the parent; `fill` grows to fill the room left in a row beside other items (it can shrink to nothing, so buttons stay on the line); `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` are fixed; `auto` adds no width class, so the control is as wide as the browser makes it.

Kbd.name: Kbd
Kbd.description: A keyboard key. Its border takes the surrounding text colour, so it reads on a filled button and on plain text.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

KeyValue.name: KeyValue
KeyValue.description:
One row of a KeyValueList: a label on the left, a tabular value on the right (or beside it, in an
`align="start"` list). `total` makes it the sum row: a rule above, strong text. `tone` colours the
value, on any row: a total that does not reconcile is `total tone="warn"`. While `loading`, a
label or value not here yet is a bone.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The term, on the left.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning of the value, in the colours of a `Table` cell's `tone` (`TextTone`; `neutral`, the default, is the list's ink); the label keeps its ink. Colour alone does not say it, so the value or the label says it too: a sign, a word.

props.name: total
props.description: The sum the rows above add up to: a firm rule above it and the label and value in strong ink.

KeyValueList.name: KeyValueList
KeyValueList.description:
A definition list of label/value rows. By default each label is on the left and its value
right-aligned. `align="start"` puts every value left-aligned in one column beside the labels,
which are sized to the widest. While `loading` with no rows it draws three rows of bones.

props.name: align
props.description: `end` right-aligns each value; `start` puts every value left-aligned in one column beside the labels, sized to the widest.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Lead.name: Lead
Lead.description: The supporting sentence under a `Display`. `p`, text-lg/7 normal, secondary.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; each role has a semantic default.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Legend.name: Legend
Legend.description:
A key to the colours of a chart or a row stripe: a swatch in the `VizTone` colour (a filled
dot, or a dashed ring with `swatch="dashed"`), its `label` and an optional `detail` after it. Colour alone does not say it, so the label is always drawn.
`StackedBar legend` draws one under the bar from its segments.
While `loading` with no `items` it draws three entries of bones.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: One entry per colour: its `label`, its `tone`, an optional `swatch` and `detail` (a count, a share).

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Lightbox.name: Lightbox
Lightbox.description:
A full-screen photo or video viewer on the browser's own `<dialog>`: it is opened with
`showModal()` on mount, so render it only while it is open. The page behind goes inert, Esc
closes it and focus stays inside; a click on the scrim around the media and its text closes it
too. The scrim stays near-black with light text in every theme. `onPrevious` and `onNext` add
step buttons and the arrow keys.

props.name: caption
props.description: Muted text on the scrim under the media.

props.name: children
props.description: The media: one `` or `

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name, for an app in another language.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The viewer's accessible name, e.g. "Photo from Anna".

props.name: meta
props.description: A muted line under the title, e.g. when.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The next button's name.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the viewer closes: Esc, a click on the scrim or the close button.

props.name: onNext
props.description: Shows a next button and binds ArrowRight. Leave it out at the last item.

props.name: onPrevious
props.description: Shows a previous button and binds ArrowLeft. Leave it out at the first item.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The previous button's name.

props.name: title
props.description: A line on the scrim above the media, e.g. who posted it.

LinkProvider.name: LinkProvider
LinkProvider.description:
Names the app's router link once, so every part that links (`Button`, `IconButton`, `TextLink`,
`Pill`, `Card`, `ListRow`, `Breadcrumbs`, `Tabs`, `SegmentedControl`, `AppShellBrand`,
`SiteSearch`, `MediaTile`, `Avatar` and the status pages) takes a plain `href` and draws an in-app
one (a path from the root, `/quotes?page=2#top`) through the router. It renders no element.

- TanStack Router: `createRouter({ routeTree, InnerWrap: ({ children }) => <LinkProvider link={(p) => <Link to="." {...p} />}>{children}</LinkProvider> })`,
  which also reaches the router's not-found and error components. A registered router's `Link`
  requires `to`; `to="."` satisfies it, and the `href` wins.
- React Router: `<LinkProvider link={({ href, ...p }) => <Link to={href} {...p} />}>` inside the router.
- Astro, or no router: no provider; every link is a plain `<a>`.

An `external` link, a full URL (`https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`), a `//` URL, a `#hash` or a relative
path never reaches the adapter: the library draws those as a plain `<a>`.

`home` is where every status page's "Back to home" goes, `/` by default: the one place an app
says it, never a page. A full URL (a home on another site) is a plain `<a>` in the same tab. A
provider inside another keeps what it does not set, so `<LinkProvider home="/app">` within the
router's provider still draws through the router's link.

props.name: home
props.description: Where the status pages' "Back to home" goes: an in-app path or a full URL.

props.name: link
props.description: The app's router link, handed `LinkAdapterProps`. Left out, links are plain `<a>` (or the outer provider's).

ListLayout.name: ListLayout
ListLayout.description: A list page: header, an optional `filters` slot, then the list, or `empty` when there are no children. While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too. With no children yet it draws a card of row bones, never `empty`.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right of the title on `sm` and up, below it on a phone.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: empty
props.description: Shown in place of `children` when there are none (no rows, an empty array, `null`): an `EmptyState`.

props.name: filters
props.description: A row between the header and the list, e.g. a `Fieldset` of chips or an `Input type="search"`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

ListRow.name: ListRow
ListRow.description:
A full-width row that runs `onClick` (or, with `href`, opens a link) with a hover
fill, a left-aligned label and `trailing` content at the far end. The row is a `<div>` with its
`<button>` or link stretched over it, so a tap anywhere on the row runs it; a `TextLink`,
`Button` or `Checkbox` in the row (in `trailing`, say a "View" link on a row that selects) sits
above it and is clickable on its own. A button row's button is named by the label alone. With `expanded` it is the header of a
collapsible section: `aria-expanded` and a chevron. Rows sit in a `Card flush`, in a
`Stack divided` that draws the line between them.

`secondary` is a second, muted line under the label. `leading` is content before the label (`leadingWidth="thumbnail"` gives it a fixed picture width),
`selected` marks the row in view, `focused` the one the keyboard cursor is on and `highlighted` fills
the row a list follows (`onPointerEnter`, `onPointerLeave` and `onFocus` reach
every form; on a button or linked row the pointer handlers go on the row itself). The label is a
`<div>`, so it can hold block content (a name over a path). A row with no `href` and no
`onClick` is a plain `<div>` with no action of its own, for one that holds its own buttons:
`actions` follow `trailing`, always shown, so a touch, a keyboard and a pointer find them alike. Such a row
also takes a `panel`, content under the row that starts where the label does (a conversation
that opens under its chat); in a `Stack divided` the line sits above the whole row, panel included. Inside a row a `Stack` is `xs` apart, and a `sm`
row makes the buttons in it `sm`. While `loading` an empty label is a bone, and what the row holds
waits with it.

props.name: actions
props.description:
Buttons for this row, after `trailing`: `Button size="sm"`, `IconButton`, a `Menu`. Always
shown: an action that shows only on hover is one a touch or keyboard user cannot find.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description: Why the row cannot be pressed: it fades, `aria-disabled` and focusable, the reason its tooltip.

props.name: expanded
props.description:
Makes the row a collapsible header: sets `aria-expanded` and shows a chevron that turns down
when open. The caller owns the state and the section; pass `aria-controls` to name it.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: focused
props.description:
Marks the row the keyboard cursor is on, for a list moved with the arrow keys or `j`/`k` while
focus stays on the list: the focus ring, drawn inside the row. It says nothing to a screen
reader (move real focus for that) and combines with `selected`.

props.name: highlighted
props.description:
Marks the row a list follows with the pointer and the keyboard alike (set it from
`onPointerEnter` and `onFocus`): a fill one step deeper than hover, so it shows on a white card
and on a tinted panel alike. It is the only fill a static row takes. `selected` wins.

Clear it from `onPointerLeave`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the row a link to this URL; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: leading
props.description: Content before the label: an Avatar, a thumbnail, an icon.

props.name: leadingWidth
props.description: A fixed width for `leading`, for a thumbnail (an `` fills it), so the labels of rows with and without a picture still line up. Without it `leading` is as wide as its content. For a row that shows a screenshot.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: onClick
props.description: What the row does when pressed: it makes the row a button.

props.name: onPointerEnter
props.description: On the row, not its link or button, so a link or button in the row does not count as entering it.

props.name: onPointerLeave
props.description: On the row, not its link or button, so a link or button in the row does not count as leaving it.

props.name: panel
props.description:
Content under the row, lined up with the label rather than the row's edge (past `leading`): the
panel of a row that opens in place, such as a conversation under its chat. It sits inside the
row, so the fill and a `Stack divided` line cover it too. Only a row that is neither a
button nor a link takes it.

props.name: secondary
props.description: A second, muted line under the label (a date, a note), like `TableCell`'s `secondary`.

props.name: selected
props.description:
Marks the row in view, the one whose detail is open: an accent fill and `aria-current="true"`.
Set it on one row of a list.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is dense padding, `lg` one step roomier than `md`. A `Button`, `IconButton` or `Pill` in a
`sm` row with no `size` of its own is `sm` too.

props.name: stripe
props.description:
The row's status, as a stripe on its leading edge in this tone, as a `Table` row's `stripe`. The
colour says it to the eye only, so the row's words say it too (a `Pill`, a status in `trailing`).

props.name: trailing
props.description: Content at the far end of the row: a value, a count, a Pill.

Maintenance.name: Maintenance
Maintenance.description:
The site is down on purpose and will be back: the page for planned downtime, such as an upgrade.
A failure is an `ErrorPage`, and no connection is `Offline`. It has no "Back to home": home is
the site that is down.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to add a button; `homeLabel` and `retryLabel` only reword the built-in ones.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

Mark.name: Mark
Mark.description:
A highlighted run inside text: a `<mark>`, on the warn tint, such as the words a search matched
in a result. It takes the surrounding size and weight. Mark the words that matter to what the
reader is doing, not emphasis: that is `Text strong`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

Markdown.name: Markdown
Markdown.description:
A small, safe Markdown renderer for notes and for rich text from a CMS: `## ` and `### `
headings, `- ` or `* ` bullets, `1. ` numbered lists, `**bold**`, `[links](href)`, a picture on a
line of its own (`![alt](src)`), GFM tables and paragraphs. Text is rendered as React nodes, never
as HTML. A link is a `TextLink` (an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`) and is kept only if
its address is a web, mail or phone address or a path on this site; any other (`javascript:`)
keeps its words and drops the link. A picture is an `Image` in its own shape, and a table a
`Table` named by the heading above it, or `tableLabel`. While `loading` with no `md` yet it
draws a paragraph of bones.

A `## ` heading is one level below the heading that holds the Markdown (an `h2` on the page, an
`h3` in a `Section`, an `h4` in a titled `Card` there) and a `### ` one below that, never past
`h6`, so the notes keep the page's outline.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: md
props.description: The Markdown source; while `loading`, none yet is a paragraph of bones.

props.name: tableLabel
props.description: The name a table takes when no heading comes before it, for an app in another language.

MediaTile.name: MediaTile
MediaTile.description:
A thumbnail tile: a picture in a fixed shape with an optional label on its bottom edge and a
caption under it. With `onClick` the whole tile is one button, which is how a grid or a
`ScrollStrip` of media opens each item in a `Lightbox`. The label sits on the same near-black
media scrim as the Lightbox, in every theme. The thumbnail is cropped to fill its shape, or with
`aspect="natural"` shown whole. With `href` the whole tile is one link instead. `onRemove` adds a
remove button for a tile that can be taken back out. `badge` pins a short word to a top corner.
While `loading` with no `src` yet the picture is a bone of its shape.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the thumbnail shows; it is the tile's name, with `label`.

props.name: aspect
props.description:
The shape of the thumbnail, as `Image`'s `aspect`; `natural` keeps the picture's own
proportions (a chat image) and crops nothing.

props.name: badge
props.description:
A short word pinned to the picture's top-right corner on the media scrim: a count, "New" or a
size. Text only; it is part of the tile's name. With `onRemove` the button takes that corner,
so the badge sits top-left.

props.name: caption
props.description: Muted text under the picture, e.g. when.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the whole tile one link, named as the button form is; an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: A short line on the bottom edge of the picture, on the media scrim: who posted it, or "Earlier".

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: onClick
props.description:
Makes the whole tile one button; open a `Lightbox` from it. Without it (or `href`) the
tile is a plain, non-interactive block.

props.name: onRemove
props.description:
Adds a round remove button on the picture's top-right corner, named `removeLabel` and `alt`: a
photo attached to a form, until it is sent. It is its own button, beside the tile's, so a tile
with `onClick` still opens its `Lightbox`.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: The remove button's word, before `alt` in its name and alone as its tooltip.

props.name: src
props.description: The thumbnail, a local path or a data URL. Left out, or if it fails to load, a placeholder shows.

props.name: video
props.description: Draws a play mark on the thumbnail: the tile opens a video, not a photo. Say so in `alt` too.

props.name: width
props.description: `sm` 96px, `md` 160px, `lg` 256px or `xl` 448px wide; `full` fills the parent (a tile in a grid).

Menu.name: Menu
Menu.description:
A button that opens a short list of actions: the overflow menu at the end of a row, a card header
or a page header. Keep the one main action in view beside it and put the rest here, the `danger`
one last. `items` are data: each a `label` with `onClick`, or a link with `href` (`external` for
a new tab), an optional leading `icon`, `tone="danger"` and `disabledReason`. `open` and
`onOpenChange` hold it open from the app's own state.

`trigger="icon"` (the default) is a ghost three-dot button named by `label`; `trigger="button"` is
an outline button reading `label`. The menu opens below the trigger, aligned to its end, and flips
when there is no room. The keyboard is the menu button pattern: Enter, Space or ArrowDown open it
on the first item, ArrowUp on the last; the arrows, Home, End and a letter move; Enter chooses;
Escape closes, and focus goes back to the trigger. `data-*` and `aria-*` land on the trigger.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Opens on mount, for a story or a test that shows the open menu.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The actions, in order.

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger's accessible name and the menu's. With `trigger="button"` it is the visible text.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Runs with the new state when the trigger, Escape, a click outside or a choice opens or shuts it.

props.name: open
props.description:
Holds the menu open or shut from the app's own state (a keyboard shortcut that opens it). Pass
`onOpenChange` with it, or the trigger, Escape and a choice cannot change it.

props.name: size
props.description:
The trigger's height, the same steps as `IconButton` and `Button`: `sm` inside a row or a card
header. The menu's own text does not change with it.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
`icon` is a ghost square button holding three dots, the overflow menu; `button` is an outline
`Button` with `label` as its text and a chevron after it, for a menu whose name is worth a word.

MetaList.name: MetaList
MetaList.description:
A wrapping row of facts or links in muted small text, joined by a `·`: branch · SHA · date, or a
footer's Privacy · Terms · Email. An item is text, a `Code` or a `TextLink`. The separator is
`aria-hidden` and leads every item in a slot of its own; the list starts one slot before its box,
which clips it, so the separator of whichever item starts a line falls outside and no line starts
or ends with one, at any width. `separator` swaps it for a `•` or none. An item never breaks
inside itself: the row wraps between items. `mono` sets the whole row in the monospace face, for ids and paths.
While `loading` with no items it draws three word-sized bones.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: The whole row in the monospace face, for ids and paths.

props.name: separator
props.description: The mark between items: `·`, `•`, or `none` for a gap alone.

Morph.name: Morph
Morph.description:
An element that grows into its counterpart on the next page, and shrinks back on Back, through
the View Transitions API. Wrap the card in the list and the element on the detail page, each with
the same `name` and the record's id as `item`: the browser morphs one into the other over 450 ms. The same
`name` and `item` may appear only once on a page; two on one page and the browser skips the
morph, so a list passes each record's own id. The morph runs only when the change is wrapped in a
view transition: `startPageTransition`, or a router's own option (TanStack Router
`defaultViewTransition: true` on `createRouter`, or `viewTransition` on a `Link`; React Router's
`viewTransition`, Astro's `ClientRouter`). Otherwise, or where the browser has no View
Transitions, it renders and behaves as a plain `<div>`. Inside a `PageFade` the page fades while
this element morphs. While it is named (near the screen) the div is a stacking context, so a
dropdown inside it cannot rise above a sticky header outside it: portal overlays to the body. Under
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it swaps with no animation; a router's own transition of the
rest of the page is the router's to quiet. A Morph more than a screen above or below the viewport
carries no transition name until it scrolls near, so a long list costs only what is on screen.
In a list, `as="li"` makes it the list's item. When one record shows twice on a page, pass
`active={false}` to the copy that should not morph; in development two active Morphs with the
same `name` and `item` log a console warning.

props.name: active
props.description:
Whether it carries its transition name; `true` by default. Pass `false` to every copy but one
when the same record shows twice on a page (a featured card and the same card in the list), so
only the one that should grow into the detail is named.

props.name: as
props.description:
The element it renders: `"div"` (the default), or `"li"` for a card that is an item of a list,
so the list stays a `ul` of `li`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: item
props.description: Which one, usually the record's id. Any text or number; unique on the page for one `name`.

props.name: name
props.description: What the element is, shared by the card and its detail: `"shop"`, `"product"`. Any text.

NavigationProgress.name: NavigationProgress
NavigationProgress.description:
A thin indeterminate bar along the top edge of the viewport, in the accent tone, for a route
change that is under way and has no known length. Pass `loading` from the router's pending state
and render it once per app, beside the page frame. It draws exactly what `loading` says: the bar
while it is true and nothing while it is false. The stylesheet holds it invisible for the first
150ms, so a fast navigation shows nothing. It is fixed to the viewport and overlays the top of
the header, so nothing on the page moves. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the segment
slides slowly and evenly instead: a still, full bar would read as finished.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The bar's accessible name.

props.name: loading
props.description: True while a navigation is pending, e.g. from the router's state.

NotFound.name: NotFound
NotFound.description:
404: the page is not there. `numeral` draws a large "404" above the title, for a site whose 404
is a designed page; the digits are fixed. Off, the page is the title and copy alone.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to add a button; `homeLabel` and `retryLabel` only reword the built-in ones.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: homeLabel
props.description: The button to the `LinkProvider`'s `home`, for an app in another language.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: numeral
props.description: Draws a large "404" above the title. Off by default. The digits are fixed: there is no text prop.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

NumberField.name: NumberField
NumberField.description:
A number with a minus and a plus button either side of it, for a quantity, a count or an amount:
React Aria's `NumberField`. The person types the number or steps it by `step` with the buttons,
the arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down; `minValue` and `maxValue` stop the buttons and clamp a
typed number when the field is left. `formatOptions` writes it as a currency, a percent or with
fixed decimals in the app's locale, and the person types in that format. `label`, `hint`, `error`,
`required` and `disabled` are a `DateField`'s; `size` and `width` an `Input`'s. While `loading`
the label is drawn and the field is a bone of its height.

props.name: decrementLabel
props.description: The name of the minus button, for an app in another language.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The number it starts with, uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and its buttons.

props.name: error
props.description: Marks the field invalid and shows this in red under the hint, announced politely.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description:
How the number is written, in the locale of the app's `I18nProvider` or else the browser's:
`{ style: "currency", currency: "EUR" }`, `{ style: "percent" }`, `{ maximumFractionDigits: 2 }`.
The person types in the same format.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the field that says more; it stays while an error shows under it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: incrementLabel
props.description: The name of the plus button, for an app in another language.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible label, above it. Without one, name the field with `aria-label`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The largest number allowed: the plus button stops there, and a larger typed one is lowered to it.

props.name: minValue
props.description: The smallest number allowed: the minus button stops there, and a smaller typed one is raised to it.

props.name: name
props.description: Posts the number in a form under this key, as plain digits whatever the format.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new number when it is committed (a step, or leaving the field); `NaN` when it is cleared.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the number required: the field is `aria-required`, and an empty one is invalid.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is compact, `text-sm` with less padding, for dense forms and table rows; `md` is `text-base`;
`lg` is `text-lg` with more padding, for a hero form. Under an `AppShell density="compact"` each
is one type step down, and on a touch screen a field is never under 16px.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as a `Button`'s
does: give the field and the buttons in its row the same value, so the row stays aligned.

props.name: step
props.description: How far one press of a button or an arrow key moves the number; a typed number snaps to it.

props.name: value
props.description: The number shown, controlled, with `onChange`. `NaN` is an empty field.

props.name: width
props.description: `full` (default) fills the parent; `fill` grows to fill the room left in a row beside other items (it can shrink to nothing, so buttons stay on the line); `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` are fixed; `auto` adds no width class, so the control is as wide as the browser makes it.

Offline.name: Offline
Offline.description: The device has no connection. `onRetry` adds a "Try again" button, unless `actions` replaces it.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The page's own buttons, before "Back to home", which turns outline beside them. This is the one
way to add a button; `homeLabel` and `retryLabel` only reword the built-in ones.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the default body copy.

props.name: homeLabel
props.description: The button to the `LinkProvider`'s `home`, for an app in another language.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Adds a "Try again" button that calls it, unless `actions` replaces the button.

props.name: retryLabel
props.description: The button `onRetry` adds, for an app in another language.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the default heading.

OutlineRegion.name: OutlineRegion
OutlineRegion.description:
An accent outline over one area of a picture, such as a screenshot's ignored or flagged region.
`rect` is in the picture's own units and `within` is the picture's full size in the same units;
the box is placed in percent of them, so it sits right at any scale. Put it in a `RegionFrame`,
over the picture. `label` is a small tag in its top-left
corner; `hatched` stripes the inside, for an area that is left out. It takes no pointer events,
so it never blocks the picture or a layer drawn over it.

`tone` colours it by what the area is (`positive`, `warn`, `danger`; `accent` by default),
`dashed` draws the edge dashed, for an area that is proposed or approximate, and `active` draws a
thicker edge, for the one region the app has picked (the one hovered in a list beside the
picture, say). The app sets `active`; the region has no hover state of its own.

props.name: active
props.description: Draws a thicker edge, for the region the app has picked. The app sets it; there is no hover state.

props.name: dashed
props.description: Draws the edge dashed, for an area that is proposed or approximate.

props.name: hatched
props.description: Stripes the inside, for an area left out (ignored, masked).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: A short tag in the top-left corner: where the area came from, or what it is.

props.name: rect
props.description: The area, in the picture's own units.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour: `accent`, `positive`, `warn` or `danger`.

props.name: within
props.description: The picture's full size, in the same units as `rect`.

Overline.name: Overline
Overline.description:
Small all-caps label above a group. `span`, text-xs semibold uppercase, tertiary. `tone`,
`numeric`, `mono` and `align` are opt-in, as on `Text`.

props.name: align
props.description:
Set the text at `start`, `center` or `end` of its block. The run becomes block-level, so the
alignment has a box to act on (a table header cell, a right-hand column).

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; each role has a semantic default.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: The monospace face, for an id, a path or a command.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures, so a column of amounts lines up.

props.name: tone
props.description:
The ink: `neutral`, the default, is the role's own; `muted` and `accent` set the hierarchy of
the text; `positive`, `warn`, `danger` and `info` say what a run means (see `TextTone`).

PageFade.name: PageFade
PageFade.description:
