The page's content area, cross-faded by the View Transitions API when the route changes. Wrap
what changes between pages, once per page. With no `name` the fade is the browser's own
cross-fade of the whole viewport; the frame around the content (header, footer) stays still
because it is the same on both pages. A `name` names this box so it fades apart from the page,
for a second region; a named region is captured at its full height, so name only a region no
taller than the screen, and give each named one on a page its own `name`.
The fade runs only when the navigation is wrapped in a view transition: `startPageTransition`,
or a router's own option (TanStack Router `viewTransition`, React Router's `viewTransition` prop,
Astro's `ClientRouter`). Otherwise, or where the browser has no View Transitions, it renders
and behaves as a plain `<div>`. A named PageFade is a stacking context, so a dropdown inside it
cannot rise above a sticky header outside it: portal overlays to the body. The default one is
not. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the content swaps with no fade; a named one quiets
only its own box, and a router's own transition of the rest of the page is the router's to quiet.
It is where `startPageTransition` puts the focus after the change: it takes focus from script,
never from Tab, and draws no ring for it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: name
props.description: A view-transition name for this box, a CSS identifier (letters, digits, `-`, `_`), for a region no taller than the screen that fades apart from the page.

PageHeader.name: PageHeader
PageHeader.description:
The top of a page: breadcrumbs, title, description, actions and tabs. Its fixed bottom margin puts
every page's first block at the same y; as a direct child of a `Stack` it has none, so the Stack's
gap is the only space under it.
While `loading` it is the owner of the wait: what it has is drawn and an empty title is a bone.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right of the title on `sm` and up, below it on a phone.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

PageHeading.name: PageHeading
PageHeading.description:
Page title. `h1`, text-3xl/9 bold (text-4xl/10 from `sm`), tight, primary text: well above the
`Lead` under it and the body text after it, so the page's title reads first.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; each role has a semantic default.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

Pagination.name: Pagination
Pagination.description:
Page links for a long list: Previous, the page numbers and Next, in a `<nav>` named by `label`.
Each is a link to `pageHref(page)`, drawn by the app's router link through `LinkProvider`, so the
page lives in the URL and back, a new tab and a shared link all work. The current page is a link
with `aria-current="page"`. Below `sm` the numbers give way to `pageLabel` ("Page 2 of 4").
Renders nothing for one page. The count line ("21 to 40 of 312") is the caller's `Caption`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the `<nav>`. Two pagers on a page (above and below a list) each need their own.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The next-page link's text.

props.name: page
props.description: The page shown, from 1. Drawn clamped into `1` to `pageCount`.

props.name: pageCount
props.description: How many pages there are. One or none draws nothing.

props.name: pageHref
props.description: The URL of one page, called for every link drawn: `(page) => (page > 1 ? `?page=${page}` : "?")`.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: The summary shown in place of the numbers below `sm`. Default: `Page 2 of 4`.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The previous-page link's text.

Pill.name: Pill
Pill.description:
A small tinted label whose `tone` says what it means; `dot` adds a leading dot in the pill's own
text colour, `round` swaps the rounded-md corners for a full pill shape, and `size` steps the
text (with none, it takes its container's). `name` makes it two-tone, `name: value`: the name
keeps the tone's tint and the children, the value, sit on the surface beside it. `href` makes it
a link (the app's router link through `LinkProvider` for an in-app path, else a plain `<a>`;
`external` opens a new tab) and `onClick` makes it
a button, each with a hover dim and the focus ring. `onRemove` adds an x button after the text
(named by `removeLabel`, by default `Remove` and the pill's text), a separate button beside a link or button pill rather than nested in
it. `title` is its tooltip and description; a plain pill with one takes a tab stop. While
`loading` with no text yet it is a bone of its size. Its text never wraps: a pill is one unit,
so keep it to a word or two.

props.name: children
props.description: The pill's text; while `loading`, none yet draws the pill as a bone of its size.

props.name: dot
props.description: A leading dot in the pill's own text colour.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab: adds `target="_blank"` and `rel="noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the pill a link to this URL; an in-app path goes through the app's `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: name
props.description:
The name half of a two-tone `name: value` pill: `children` is the value. The name keeps the
tone's tint and the value sits on a plain surface beside it, in a hairline border. Keep the
name to a word or two (`Weight`, `Sleep`).

props.name: onClick
props.description: A Pill that is a button: runs `onClick`. Defaults to `type="button"`.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Adds a small x button after the text that calls this: for a chip the reader can drop (an attachment, a filter). It sits beside a link or button pill, never inside it.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description:
The x button's whole accessible name and tooltip: `Remove invoice.pdf`. Left out, it is
`Remove` followed by the pill's text when that text is a string or a number, else `Remove`.

props.name: round
props.description: A full pill shape in place of the rounded-md corners.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is smaller text, for a dense row; `lg` larger, beside a heading. Left out, a Pill takes
the size of the `Card`, `ListRow` or `Table` it sits in, else `md`.

props.name: title
props.description:
The detail behind a pill whose text is short or cut off (the full status, a date): its tooltip
on hover, keyboard focus and a tap, and its description. A plain pill with a title is focusable.

Keep anything a reader needs on the pill itself.

props.name: tone
props.description:
What the pill means: `neutral`, `info`, `positive`, `warn` or `danger`, or `accent` for a
category that is none of those.

Popover.name: Popover
Popover.description:
A button that opens a small panel of content beside it: a detail, a short list, a filter. It is
the browser's own popover, rendered in place: a click outside it, Esc or the trigger closes it,
and the focus goes back to the trigger. It is not modal: the page stays usable, and Tab moves from
the trigger into the panel and on. A list of actions is a `Menu`; a question to answer first is a
`Dialog`. `data-*` and `aria-*` land on the trigger.

props.name: children
props.description: What the panel holds: a few lines, a short list, a filter or two.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Opens on mount, for a story or a test that shows the open panel.

props.name: icon
props.description:
Makes the trigger a ghost square button holding this glyph, named by `label` (shown as its
tooltip). Without it the trigger is an outline `Button` reading `label`, with a chevron.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger's accessible name and the panel's. Without `icon` it is the trigger's visible text.

props.name: size
props.description:
The trigger's height, the same steps as `IconButton` and `Button`: `sm` inside a row or a card
header. The panel does not change with it.

Price.name: Price
Price.description:
A price as the page already formatted it ("R52"), in tabular figures so a column of prices lines
up. With `was` the old price follows it struck through, and a screen reader hears "R52, was R65",
since a strike says nothing out loud. It formats nothing: the app owns the currency and the
locale. While `loading` with no `value` yet it is a bone of its size.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` for a dense row, `md` for a tile, `lg` for a product's own page.

props.name: value
props.description: The price, formatted for the reader ("R52", "€12.50"). While `loading`, none yet is a bone.

props.name: was
props.description: The price before a sale, struck through after `value`.

ProductTile.name: ProductTile
ProductTile.description:
One thing for sale in a shop's grid: its picture, its name and its `Price` (with the was price
on a sale), and a corner word for `sale` or `sold-out`. The whole tile is one link to the
product's page, named by what it says: "Linen shirt, R52, was R65, Sale". The picture is
decoration, since the name says what it is. It fills its column, so a set of them goes in a
`CardGrid`. While `loading` the picture, the name and the price that are not here yet are bones.

props.name: aspect
props.description: The picture's shape: `square` for most things, `3:4` for clothes on a person.

props.name: href
props.description: The product's page; an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: name
props.description: The product's name, the tile's first words. While `loading`, none yet is a bone.

props.name: price
props.description: The price, formatted by the app ("R52"), as `Price`'s `value`.

props.name: src
props.description: The product's picture. Left out, or if it fails to load, the picture's placeholder shows.

props.name: status
props.description: A word on the picture's top-left corner: `sale`, or `sold-out` when there are none left.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: The corner's word, for an app in another language.

props.name: was
props.description: The price before the sale, struck through after `price`.

ProgressBar.name: ProgressBar
ProgressBar.description:
A thin horizontal bar with a filled share, for progress toward a total. `value` is held
between 0 and `max`. `label` names what it measures, for a screen reader, which also hears the percentage.
While `loading` it is one bone the bar's size, since 0 is a real value.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar measures, for a screen reader, which also hears the percentage.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: max
props.description: The value that fills the bar; `value` is drawn as its share of this. Defaults to 100.

props.name: size
props.description: The bar's height: `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 12px.

props.name: tone
props.description:
What the progress means: `accent` (the default) plain progress, `positive` done or on track,
`warn` at risk, `danger` over a limit or failed.

props.name: value
props.description: How far along, held between 0 and `max`.

PromoBanner.name: PromoBanner
PromoBanner.description:
A slim full-width strip that carries one offer and one action: "Refills from R390 this week",
then "Shop refills". It is the theme's accent fill with its label colour, and the action is a
small surface pill on it, so both hold AA contrast in every theme. Put it above the `AppShell`'s
header or as the first block of the page; one per page. The words wrap and stay centred on a
phone. With `href` the action is a link (an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`), with
`onClick` a button.

props.name: action
props.description: The action's words: "Shop refills".

props.name: children
props.description: The offer, one short line: "Refills from R390 this week".

props.name: href
props.description: Where the action goes; an in-app path goes through `LinkProvider`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: onClick
props.description: The action as a button instead of a link: it opens a dialog, say.

Prose.name: Prose
Prose.description:
Long-form content, for a docs page or an article. A block (`div`) that sets the long line height
(leading-7) on itself and puts the text roles inside it on the prose scale: `Text` text-base/7
(the size it is outside, on a longer line), `SectionHeading` text-2xl/8, `SubsectionHeading` `lg` text-2xl/8,
`md` text-xl/7 and `sm` text-base/7 (a semibold line at body size), and the box of a `Callout`
text-base/7. Every other role keeps its size. Nothing outside a `Prose` changes, and a `Dialog`,
`Drawer` or `EmptyState` inside one is back on the app scale. An app screen never uses it: wrap the
body of a docs page or an article, inside a `ProseLayout`, a `SidebarLayout` or anywhere else.
Its blocks (`Section`s, paragraphs) are a `Stack`'s gap apart, as they would be in a `Stack`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

ProseLayout.name: ProseLayout
ProseLayout.description:
A text page: header, then `children` stacked `gap` apart (`md` by default), all in one column that
starts at the Container's start edge (it is not re-centred, so the title does not jump). `width`
sets the column: `narrow` (`max-w-3xl`, the default) is a reading measure; `wide` (`max-w-5xl`) and
`full` (the Container's whole width) suit a page that is not long prose, such as a pricing page.
Paragraphs (`Text`) and the header's lede keep their own reading measure whatever the width.
Unlike `FormLayout` the header sits inside the column, so its `actions` stay beside the text
instead of at the Container's far edge. While `loading` it owns the wait and passes it to everything inside, the header too.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right of the title on `sm` and up, below it on a phone.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: A `Breadcrumbs` above the title.

props.name: description
props.description: The lede under the title: a `Lead`, so it outranks the body text after it.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between blocks: `xs` gap-2, `sm` gap-4, `md` gap-6, `lg` gap-8, `xl` gap-12 (gap-16 from `sm`).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tabs
props.description: A `Tabs` (or similar) under the title.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's `h1`.

props.name: width
props.description: The column's width, as a `Stack`'s: `narrow` max-w-3xl, `wide` max-w-5xl, `full` the Container's width.

Radio.name: Radio
Radio.description: One option of a `RadioGroup`: a `label` and, under it, an optional `hint`. Click the label or the circle. While `loading` the circle is a bone.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables this radio alone.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the label that says more. It is the radio's `aria-describedby`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the circle.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: value
props.description: What the group's `value` becomes when this one is chosen.

RadioGroup.name: RadioGroup
RadioGroup.description:
A named group of radios, one chosen. The `label` names the group; `hint` is a muted line under
the options that says more (the group's description); an `error` adds a red line with an alert
icon under it, announced politely, and marks the group invalid. `required` puts a red asterisk
after the label. Give it `value` and `onChange`, or
`defaultValue` and let it keep the choice. `name` posts the choice in a form.
The arrow keys move between the radios and choose, and the group is one tab stop. `size` sizes
every radio in the group, the same scale as a `Checkbox`. `variant="card"` draws each radio as an
option card: a bordered box, its label the title and its hint the description, the chosen one
with an accent edge. While `loading` the labels are drawn and each circle is a bone.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Radio`s.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The `value` chosen to begin with, when the group keeps its own choice.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every radio.

props.name: error
props.description: A red line under the hint, with an alert icon; marks the group invalid. Like `Field`'s `error`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the options that says more; it describes the group, and stays while `error` shows.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible name, above the options.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field the choice posts under.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the chosen radio's `value`.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the choice required: a red asterisk after the label, the group is `aria-required`, and a form will not submit with no option chosen.

props.name: size
props.description:
The size of every radio in the group: `sm` is `text-xs` and a smaller circle, `lg` `text-base`
and a larger one.

props.name: value
props.description: The `value` of the chosen radio.

props.name: variant
props.description:
`plain` is a column of circles and their words. `card` makes each radio a bordered box the
width of the group, its label a title and its `hint` the description: for a few options that
each need a line of explaining (a plan, a delivery speed). The whole card is the click target.

readColourScheme.name: readColourScheme
readColourScheme.description: The stored choice, else the system preference. `fallback` (default `"light"`) is for when neither is available: server rendering, or storage that throws with no `matchMedia`.

refreshMorphs.name: refreshMorphs
refreshMorphs.description:
Measures every mounted Morph again, at once, so a card a router has just scrolled on screen
carries its transition name before the browser captures the new page. Call it right after the
router restores scroll, when that happens after the render: TanStack Router restores scroll on
`onRendered`, a few microtasks after the commit, which is too late for Morph to see on its own.

```ts
const router = createRouter({ routeTree, defaultViewTransition: true, scrollRestoration: true });
router.subscribe("onRendered", () => refreshMorphs());
```

Subscribe after the router is created, so its own scroll restore runs first. A restore in a
layout effect, during the commit, needs no call. It takes no arguments and does nothing on the
server or where there is no IntersectionObserver.

RegionFrame.name: RegionFrame
RegionFrame.description: A picture with a hairline edge, and `children` laid over it: the `OutlineRegion`s that mark its areas. `onLoad`, `id`, `data-*` and `aria-*` go to the ``, so the app can read the picture's own size for `within`. While `loading` with no `src` yet it is a bone of the frame's shape (4:3 for a `natural` one), as an `Image` is. It sizes as `Image` does. `width` is `full` (the parent's width) or 96, 160 or 256px. `aspect` `natural` keeps the picture's own proportions; any other shape letterboxes it (contain, never a crop) on the inset surface, centred and never scaled up, and the regions are laid over the picture itself, not the box, so each stays on its spot. A letterboxed picture needs its own size: a screenshot has one; an SVG needs `width` and `height` on its root, not only a `viewBox`.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the picture shows; `""` for one that only decorates.

props.name: aspect
props.description: The box's shape: `natural` is the picture's own; any other letterboxes the picture inside it.

props.name: children
props.description: The `OutlineRegion`s over the picture.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: src
props.description: The picture; left out while it is not known yet, with `loading`.

props.name: width
props.description: How wide the frame is: `full` fills its parent; `sm`, `md` and `lg` are 96, 160 and 256px, capped at the parent's width.

schemeClass.name: schemeClass
schemeClass.description: The class for `scheme`: what to render on `<html>` on the server so the first paint is right. `""` for the default light scheme.

ScrollStrip.name: ScrollStrip
ScrollStrip.description:
A single row of items that scrolls sideways when it runs past the width of its parent, with a
themed scrollbar and the items snapping into place: a strip of `MediaTile`s or `Avatar`s.
Items never shrink or wrap. The strip takes the keyboard focus, so the arrow keys scroll it
without a pointer. A grid that wraps is a `CardGrid` or a `Cluster`.

props.name: children
props.description: The items, one after another: `MediaTile`s, `Avatar`s. They keep their own width.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between items, as `Cluster`'s `gap`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the strip for a screen reader, e.g. "Recent statuses".

Section.name: Section
Section.description:
A `<section>` Stack with an optional title (which names it) and `actions`. Its blocks are `gap`
apart, from where it sits as in a `Stack`. `level` is the title's heading level, one below the
heading that holds the section (an `h2` on the page), and a heading inside it (a `Card`'s title)
is one below that. A line between two sections is a `Divider` in the `Stack` that holds them.

`size` picks the scale:
- `md` (default): a page's section. A `SectionHeading` title with `actions` at the end of its row;
  `rule` draws a hairline under the row, `overline` a small label above the title and
  `description` a muted line under it.
- `sm`: the small titled group inside a page, a card, a drawer or a side panel (a panel's "Flaky"
  block, a card's "Ignore areas"): the title small and all-caps like a `Card`'s, the blocks `xs`
  apart. Never build one from a `Stack as="section"` and an `Overline`.
- `lg`: a landing page's section under the `Hero`: a mono `overline` kicker, the title at display
  size, `description` as a `Lead` and `actions` under it as its calls to action, the opening
  capped at the reading measure at the start edge, the blocks `lg` apart. It ignores the prose scale.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons or links: at the end of the title row, or under the description at `size="lg"`.

props.name: description
props.description: The line under the title, outside the heading: a muted line at `md`, a `Lead` at `lg`.

props.name: gap
props.default: xs at `size="sm"`, lg at `size="lg"`; else xs inside a `Card`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`, `Callout` or `ListRow`, else md
props.description: The space between blocks: `xs` gap-2, `sm` gap-4, `md` gap-6, `lg` gap-8, `xl` gap-12 (gap-16 from `sm`).

props.name: id
props.description:
Makes the section a link target: `#<id>` scrolls to its heading, which stops below the sticky
AppShell header, as every `id` inside the shell does; write no `scroll-margin`. Needs a `title`:
with no title the heading that carries it is not rendered.
The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: level
props.default: one below the heading that holds the section: 2 on the page
props.description: The title's heading level, 2 to 6. It does not change how the title looks.

props.name: overline
props.description: A small label above the title, in the same `<header>` (mono at `size="lg"`). Needs a `title`.

props.name: rule
props.description:
A hairline under the title row across the section's width, `actions` included. Needs a
`title` or `actions`.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` a small titled group inside a page, a card or a panel, its title small and all-caps
and its blocks `xs` apart; `md` a page's section; `lg` a landing page's section, a display
title under a mono kicker, a `Lead`, then its calls to action.

A landing page's section under the `Hero` is `size="lg"`: its opening is capped at the
reading measure at the start edge and its blocks sit `lg` apart. A feature card in it is
a `Card href icon titleStyle="name"` in a `CardGrid`; text beside code is a `SideColumn`.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading at the top, which names the section.

props.name: width
props.description:
Caps the column: `compact` max-w-md (one card or one picture's column), `narrow` max-w-3xl (a
reading measure), `wide` max-w-5xl, `full` the parent's whole width, `default` sets nothing.

SectionHeading.name: SectionHeading
SectionHeading.description:
Top-level section header. `h2`, text-xl/7 semibold, primary text (text-base/6 under an
`AppShell density="compact"`, text-2xl/8 semibold tight inside a `Prose`). `rule` sets
a hairline under it (the `Divider` line colour) with the space either side of
the line built in. `description` is a muted line under the heading, outside the `<h2>`, so the
heading's name stays the title; the rule then sits under the description.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; each role has a semantic default.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted line under the heading that says more. It is a paragraph beside the heading, not part of its name.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: rule
props.description: A hairline under the heading, with the space either side of it built in.

SegmentedControl.name: SegmentedControl
SegmentedControl.description:
A joined pill group where one option is filled: a mode or a range chosen in place. `items` are
`{ value, label }` buttons (`value` and `onChange` are the caller's state; the arrow keys, Home
and End move the choice) or links (`href`, an in-app one drawn by the app's router `<Link>` through `LinkProvider`;
`value` marks the current one, which gets `aria-current`). An item may carry a `count`, and a
button one `disabledReason` (it stays reachable by the arrows and its reason is a tooltip) or a bare `disabled`; `disabled` on the group disables every
option. `label` names the group. `size` matches the height of a `Button` of the same size, and
`{ base, md }` changes it at 48rem.
`fill` stretches the options across the group's width; `wrap` lets them wrap into full rows of a
box, always or (`"narrow"`) only while the group is under 32rem wide.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every option is disabled, e.g. until the page has hydrated.

props.name: fill
props.description:
The group takes its parent's full width and the options grow to share it, so the border ends
at the last option. Still a pill.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The options in order: `{ value, label }` buttons, or links (`href`), the current link marked by its `selected` or by a `value` equal to the group's. Either may carry a `count`; a button may be `disabled`.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the group.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the option's `value` when one is chosen, by click or arrow key.

props.name: size
props.description:
The control's height and text, on the scale of a `Button`. `{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes
size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS.

Give it the same value as a responsive `Button` in the same row.

props.name: value
props.description: The `value` of the current option; for links, an alternative to `selected` on the item.

props.name: wrap
props.description:
The options wrap onto full rows of at most three (five are 3 then 2) in a box with rounded
corners and a line between options, instead of a pill. `"narrow"`: the box only while the group
itself is under 32rem wide (a container query, so it follows the column it sits in), and a
filled pill from 32rem up. Implies `fill`.

For five options that will not fit one row.

Select.name: Select
Select.description:
A native `<select>` styled like `Input`, keeping the browser's own arrow, over its `items`. Takes
`size` and `width` too: inside a `Field` it fills the row, and on its own it is as wide as its
longest choice. The `ref` reaches the `<select>`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the select; say why in its `Field` hint.

props.name: items
props.description: The choices, in order.

props.name: name
props.description: The key the value posts under in a form.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<select>` itself, for focus control.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is compact, `text-sm` with less padding, for dense forms and table rows; `md` is `text-base`;
`lg` is `text-lg` with more padding, for a hero form. Under an `AppShell density="compact"` each
is one type step down, and on a touch screen a field is never under 16px.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as a `Button`'s
does: give the field and the buttons in its row the same value, so the row stays aligned.

props.name: width
props.description: As an `Input`'s `width`.

Show.name: Show
Show.description:
Shows its children only from a width up (`from`) or only below it (`below`), by CSS alone: the same markup on the server and the client, with no script. Hidden is `display: none`, so the content is out of the accessibility tree and the tab order too. Shown, the wrapper adds no box, so the children sit in the parent's row, grid or Stack and take its gap. Content that only fits a wide screen is in a `Show from`; its narrow-screen form is in a `Show below` at the same breakpoint. Hidden content stays mounted, so two `Show`s of the same content mount it twice: a stateful panel shown at every width with a fold is a `SideColumn fold`. `as="span"` is for phrasing content (inside a `

` or a button row).

props.name: as
props.description: The element: `div`, or `span` inside phrasing content.

props.name: below
props.description: Shown below this width, gone from it up.

props.name: from
props.description: Shown from this width up, gone below it.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

SidebarLayout.name: SidebarLayout
SidebarLayout.description:
An `aside` of links (the rail) beside the `children` canvas, in the Container the shell already gives every
page (a plain `<AppShell>`, no `bleed`): the rail starts at the header logo's x and the canvas
ends at the header's right edge. The rail has no background and no border, so it is a list of
links on the page; a `Tabs orientation="vertical"` is its content. From `md` it is `w-56` with
the canvas filling the rest, and it stays in view under the shell's header as a long page scrolls;
a rail taller than the screen scrolls itself, so its last link is reachable. Below `md` it stacks
above the canvas and nothing sticks. A long rail sets `asideLabel`:
below `md` it then folds behind a disclosure of that name, closed, so the page comes first on a
phone, and from `md` it is the same rail; `asideLabel` also names the rail's `<aside>` landmark.
Once the page has
loaded, a rail that scrolls shows its current link (the one with `aria-current`) in view, and the
folded disclosure reads `asideLabel` and the current link's name ("All components: Button"); both
need the layout to hydrate.
While `loading` the canvas waits (the rail is navigation, drawn as itself) and the layout owns
the wait.

props.name: aside
props.description: The links beside the canvas, usually a `Tabs orientation="vertical"`.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description:
Folds the rail behind a disclosure with this name below `md` (a long rail), and names the rail's
`<aside>` landmark. Left out, the rail is always open and the aside is unnamed.

Folded, the page comes first on a phone; from `md` it is the same rail.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

SideColumn.name: SideColumn
SideColumn.description:
A main area beside a side column, in the Container the page already has: from `lg` the `aside`
is `asideWidth` on the right and `children` take the room left; below `lg` the aside stacks under
`children`. It sets no page width, padding or header of its own, so it sits inside a layout, a
`Card` or a panel. `asideWidth` is `xs` (12rem), `sm` (18rem), `md` (24rem) or `third` (one
third of the row, the main area two thirds: the split `DetailLayout` draws). A rail of links on
the left is `SidebarLayout`.

`side="start"` puts the aside on the left from `lg`, and first in reading order, so below `lg`
it stacks above `children`.

`asideLabel` names the `<aside>` landmark. `fold` is for an aside that should not take the
phone's screen: below `lg` it folds, closed, behind a native disclosure named by `asideLabel`,
and from `lg` it is the same column, always shown. The aside stays mounted while folded, so a
conversation or a draft inside it is kept.

`sticky` keeps the aside in view from `lg` as a long page scrolls: it sticks under AppShell's
header and, if it is taller than the room left, scrolls itself (a tab stop named by `asideLabel`)
so its end stays reachable.

props.name: aside
props.description: The side column: `asideWidth` wide on `side` from `lg`, stacked with `children` below it.

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: Names the `<aside>` landmark, and the disclosure when `fold` is set. Left out, the aside is unnamed.

props.name: asideWidth
props.description: The aside's width from `lg`: `xs` 12rem, `sm` 18rem, `md` 24rem, or `third`, one third of the row.

props.name: fold
props.description: Folds the aside, closed, behind a disclosure named by `asideLabel` below `lg`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: side
props.description: The aside's side from `lg`: `end` (the right) or `start` (the left, and first in reading order).

props.name: sticky
props.description:
From `lg`, keeps the aside in view under the header as the page scrolls; an aside taller than
the screen scrolls inside itself.

SiteFooter.name: SiteFooter
SiteFooter.description:
The footer a site puts in `AppShell`'s `footer` slot: the site's mark linked home with a contact
line beside it, a row of the site's own links (Privacy, Terms, GitHub), then lines of fine print.
It is not a `<footer>`: the shell draws the one `contentinfo` landmark around its slot. No link
columns, newsletter form or social icons: a site footer is this and nothing else.

props.name: brand
props.description: The site's mark (a wordmark, a logo), linked to `brandHref`. Left out, there is no brand.

props.name: brandHref
props.description: Where the brand links. Needs `brand`.

props.name: brandLabel
props.description: Names the brand link for assistive tech ("PixelSlash home"). Needs `brand`.

props.name: children
props.description: A sentence at body size beside the brand: the contact line ("Email hello@...").

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: links
props.description: The site's own links (Privacy, Terms, GitHub, a mail address), one wrapping row.

props.name: notes
props.description: Lines of fine print under the links (a licence, a trademark, a credit), one paragraph each.

SiteSearch.name: SiteSearch
SiteSearch.description:
The site's search: a header button that opens a dialog with a search field over a list of links
to the pages that match. Put it in `AppShell`'s `controls` and pass every page as `items`. Ctrl+K
(⌘ K on a Mac) opens it from anywhere on the page, and the button shows that key. Typing filters
by name, then by `keywords`, then by description; Enter opens the first result (or, with
`resultsHref`, the full results page), the arrow keys move through them, and Esc closes it and
puts focus back where it was. The field is a `<search>` landmark. Render it once per page.

props.name: allResultsLabel
props.description: The full results link's text; the typed text follows it: "See all results for tabel".

props.name: buttonLabel
props.description: The wide button's text, which is also its accessible name.

props.name: countLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears for the number of matches once something is typed.

props.name: hintLabel
props.description: The muted line under the field before anything is typed.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: Every page to search, in the order ties are listed (the rail's order).

props.name: label
props.description:
The dialog's title and the phone's icon button's accessible name: "Search components". The wide
button is named by its own text, `buttonLabel`.

props.name: noResultsLabel
props.description: The muted line when nothing matches; the typed text follows it: "No results for tabel".

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The search field's placeholder.

props.name: resultsHref
props.description:
The site's full results page for a query, built from the typed text (trimmed):
`(query) => "/search?q=" + encodeURIComponent(query)`. Given, a link to it is the last row
once something is typed, matches or not, and Enter in the field goes there.

props.name: resultsLabel
props.description: The name of the list of matches, for an app in another language.

props.name: size
props.description:
The trigger's height and text, on the scale of a `Button` and an `IconButton`, so it lines up
with the other controls in a header row.

Slider.name: Slider
Slider.description:
A range slider for one number between `min` and `max` (0 and 100 unless given), in steps of
`step`: the browser's own `<input type="range">` in the accent colour, with its value written
beside the track (`formatOptions` sets how) and read out the same way. Put it in a `Field`, which
names it and draws the hint and the error, as an `Input`. Arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and
End move it. `size` sets its height and the value's type, to line up with an `Input` of that size;
`width` is an `Input`'s. `onChange` is the input's own, on every move. The `ref` reaches the `<input>`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The number it starts with, uncontrolled. Without one it starts halfway, as the browser's does.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description:
How the value beside the track is written, in the locale of the app's `I18nProvider` or else
the browser's: `{ style: "percent" }` (for a value from 0 to 1), `{ style: "currency",
currency: "EUR" }`, `{ style: "unit", unit: "kilogram" }`. Assistive tech reads it the same way.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<input>` itself, for focus control.

props.name: size
props.description:
`sm` is compact, `text-sm` with less padding, for dense forms and table rows; `md` is `text-base`;
`lg` is `text-lg` with more padding, for a hero form. Under an `AppShell density="compact"` each
is one type step down, and on a touch screen a field is never under 16px.
`{ base: "md", md: "lg" }` changes size at the `md` breakpoint (48rem), in CSS, as a `Button`'s
does: give the field and the buttons in its row the same value, so the row stays aligned.

props.name: value
props.description: The number it holds, controlled, with `onChange`.

props.name: width
props.description: `full` (default) fills the parent; `fill` grows to fill the room left in a row beside other items (it can shrink to nothing, so buttons stay on the line); `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` are fixed; `auto` adds no width class, so the control is as wide as the browser makes it.

SortableItem.name: SortableItem
SortableItem.description:
One row of a `SortableList`: a grip handle, the title, and an optional meta line under it. A
pointer drags the row by its handle only (a drag that starts anywhere else on the row is no
drag); the handle (`reorderLabel` and the title, "Reorder <title>") is also how a keyboard or
screen reader starts a move. A title cut to one line shows in full in a tooltip on hover, on the
row's keyboard focus and on a tap.

props.name: children
props.description: A meta line under the title: `Pill`s, an `Avatar`.

props.name: id
props.description:
The item's id, reported in a move.
The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: reorderLabel
props.description: The word before `title` in the handle's accessible name: "Reorder Write the brief".

props.name: title
props.description: Its one line; also what a screen reader announces while it is dragged.

SortableList.name: SortableList
SortableList.description:
A list the user puts in order: items under section headings, moved by dragging a row or from the
keyboard (each row's grip handle, Enter, the arrow keys, Enter to drop, Escape to cancel). A drop
reports `onReorder` with the item, the section it lands in and the item it lands next to; the app
applies it to its own data. The list never reorders itself: it shows what its children say.

Its children are `SortableSection`s, or `SortableItem`s directly for a list with no sections, each
a direct child (map your data straight to them). Moving an item into another section is how the
app changes its group, such as a ticket's priority. Two lists on one page never take each other's
items.

props.name: children
props.description: `SortableSection`s, or `SortableItem`s for a list with no sections.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name, read by a screen reader.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Called once per drop with the move; apply it to your data.

SortableSection.name: SortableSection
SortableSection.description:
One group of a `SortableList` under a heading that shows its title and how many items it holds.
An empty section still takes a drop: it shows a quiet "Drop here" row in place of items.

props.name: children
props.description: Its `SortableItem`s, each a direct child. With none it shows a quiet `emptyLabel` row.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: The quiet row an empty section shows, where a drop lands.

props.name: endLabel
props.description:
The word before `title` in the name of the section's last drop place, which a screen reader
announces while a move lands there: "End of Doing".

props.name: id
props.description:
The section's id, reported as `section` in a move that lands in it.
The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading over its items.

SplitBar.name: SplitBar
SplitBar.description:
A bar split between two parties, `a` on the left and `b` on the right, each sized by its share of
`a + b`. `label` names the split for a screen reader, which hears both percentages; give `names`
(left, right) so it hears whose is whose. Put the parties' names under the bar yourself.
While `loading` it is one bone the bar's size, since 0 is a real value.

props.name: a
props.description: The left party's amount; its share is `a` over `a + b`.

props.name: b
props.description: The right party's amount; its share is `b` over `a + b`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the split is, for a screen reader, which hears it before both percentages.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: names
props.description: The left and right parties, spoken before their percentages.

props.name: size
props.description: The bar's height: `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 12px.

props.name: toneA
props.description: The left part's colour, by what it means (`accent`, `positive`, `warn` or `danger`). Defaults to "danger".

props.name: toneB
props.description: The right part's colour, by what it means (`accent`, `positive`, `warn` or `danger`). Defaults to "positive".

Stack.name: Stack
Stack.description:
A vertical column of blocks a fixed `gap` apart: `xs` between lines of text (a heading and the
line under it), `sm` inside a group, `md` between blocks, `lg` between groups, `xl` between a page's top-level blocks
(`gap-12`, `sm:gap-16`: the one responsive page rhythm). Left out, the gap comes from where the
Stack sits: `xs` inside a `Card`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`, `Callout` or `ListRow`, and
`md` on the page.

`width` caps the column: `compact` is the width of one card or one picture's column (28rem),
`narrow` is a reading measure, `wide` is wider again, `full` is the parent's whole width and
`default` sets nothing. A capped Stack starts at its parent's start edge (it is never re-centred),
so its first line lines up with every other block on the page. A width cap on any one block (a
`Card`, an `Image`) is a Stack around it.

`align="start"` keeps each child at its own width, capped at the column's (a `Button` under a
form's fields); left out, every child spans the column.

`divided` draws a line between each pair of children and sets them touching, with no gap: it is
for rows that carry their own padding (`ListRow`s in a `Card flush`). Space and a line between
blocks is a `Divider` in the Stack instead.

`rowFrom` turns the column into a row from `sm`, `md` or `lg` (a column below it): the blocks sit
side by side, `gap` apart, and a `ClusterGrow` around one of them takes the width left. Without it the
Stack is always a column; a row that is a row at every width is a `Cluster`.

`as` is a closed set: `div` (default), `section`, `form`, `ul` or `ol`. A `form` takes the form
props (`onSubmit`, `action`, `method`, `noValidate`, ...). A `ul` or `ol` is drawn with no
markers and its children are `<li>`s, as in `BulletList` and `Timeline`: the Stack does not wrap
them, so a child is one list item and `Text as="li"` or a bare `<li>` both work. A `ul` or `ol`
takes `empty` (an `EmptyState`, one muted line here), drawn in place of the list when it has no
children.

props.name: align
props.description:
Where the children sit across the column: `stretch` spans it, `start` keeps each child at its
own width (a `Button` under a form's fields).

props.name: as
props.description: The element: `div`, `section`, `form` (takes the form's props), `ul` or `ol` (no markers; each child is an `<li>`).

props.name: divided
props.description:
A line between each pair of children, which then touch (no gap): rows that carry their own
padding. Space and a line between blocks is a `Divider` in the Stack instead.

Such as `ListRow`s in a `Card flush`.

props.name: empty
props.description: Drawn in place of the list when it has no children: an `EmptyState`.

props.name: gap
props.default: xs inside a `Card`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `BottomSheet`, `Callout` or `ListRow`, else md
props.description: The space between blocks: `xs` gap-2, `sm` gap-4, `md` gap-6, `lg` gap-8, `xl` gap-12 (gap-16 from `sm`).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: rowFrom
props.description:
Turns the column into a row from this breakpoint (`sm`, `md` or `lg`), a column below it: a main
area beside a side column on a wide screen, stacked on a phone. In the row the blocks sit side by side
the same `gap` apart and are as tall as the tallest; wrap the one that takes the width left in a
`ClusterGrow`. Left out, the Stack is always a column.

props.name: width
props.description:
Caps the column: `compact` max-w-md (one card or one picture's column), `narrow` max-w-3xl (a
reading measure), `wide` max-w-5xl, `full` the parent's whole width, `default` sets nothing.

StackedBar.name: StackedBar
StackedBar.description:
A bar of any number of parts, each sized by its share of the sum, in the order given. A part with
no value is zero wide. `label` names the bar for a screen reader, which hears every part's name
and whole percent (rounded, so they may not add up to exactly 100). `legend` draws a `Legend` under the bar, each part's
label with its value, so the colours are named in words. While `loading` the bar is one bone (0
is a real value) and the key keeps the names it has, without their values.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The parts in order, each a `label`, a `value` (its share is the value over the sum) and a `tone`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, for a screen reader, which hears it before every part's name and percent.

props.name: legend
props.description: Draw the key under the bar. Defaults to false; a bar with a `quiet` part always draws it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: size
props.description: The bar's height: `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 12px.

startPageTransition.name: startPageTransition
startPageTransition.description:
Run `update` inside a view transition, so a `PageFade` cross-fades, then move the focus to the
new view (the page's `PageFade`), unless it is on a tab or a radio, which switch in place.
`update` is a synchronous state change, flushed at once as the browser needs the new DOM; for a
router's navigation, which is async, use the router's own view-transition option instead (and its
own focus handling). Where the browser has no View Transitions, or the user prefers reduced
motion, `update` just runs, and the focus moves the same. Call it from an event handler, not
during render.

StateMachine.name: StateMachine
StateMachine.description:
A state machine, drawn, with the things moving through it: each state a box, each transition an
arrow named by its event, laid out like a `FlowDiagram`. A state's `kind` sets its look and a tag
that says it: `human` takes the warn tone, `failed` the danger tone, `terminal` is muted, and
`initial` is tagged start. Its `owner` is a tag beside it.

Each of the `items` is a coloured dot with its short `id`, in the box of its `state`, which
counts them; a box shows up to nine and a `+N` for the rest. The dot's name and tooltip is its
full `label`, and with an `href` it is a link. An item whose state is not in the machine goes in
a box of its own, "Not in any state", so nothing is dropped. When an item's state changes, its
dot runs along the arrow between the two (straight across when there is none); with reduced
motion it moves at once. `active` rings the one state that is current.

`fromXState` makes `states` and `transitions` from an xstate machine.

props.name: active
props.description: The `id` of the one state to ring as current.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: items
props.description: The things in the machine, each in the state its `state` names.

props.name: label
props.description: What the machine is: its accessible name.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: states
props.description: The states, each with a unique `id`.

props.name: transitions
props.description: The moves between them. One whose `from` or `to` is not a state is not drawn.

StatTile.name: StatTile
StatTile.description:
One headline figure: an uppercase caption over a large tabular-nums value, with an optional
hint line beneath. `tone` colours the value; `accent` adds a bar across the top edge in the same
tone. `trend` draws a small line under the value in the same colour. Pass the value already
formatted. While `loading`, a `label` or `value` not here yet is a bone; the hint and the trend
are drawn only once given.

props.name: accent
props.description: A bar across the top edge in the tone's colour.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the value.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The small uppercase caption over the value.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: tone
props.description:
What the figure means: `neutral` (the default) a plain figure, `positive` good or on track,
`warn` at risk, `danger` failed or over. Say it in the text too: colour alone says nothing to a
screen reader.

props.name: trend
props.description:
The figure over time, oldest first: a sparkline under the value, in its colour, on a scale
from 0. It is decoration, so say the trend in `hint` as well.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure, already formatted, large and in tabular figures.

Step.name: Step
Step.description: One step of `Steps`: a `title` and the `children` as the detail under it, at its `Steps`' size.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: title
props.description: What to do; `children` is the detail under it.

Stepper.name: Stepper
Stepper.description:
Where the reader is in a fixed run of steps (checkout, a setup flow): each step done, current
or still to come. An ordered list named by `label`, across from `sm` and down on a phone.
`current` is the step in progress, from 1; past the last step every step is done. It shows
progress and does not navigate: the flow's own buttons move between steps.

props.name: current
props.description: The step in progress, from 1. Past the last step, every step is done.

props.name: doneLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears after a done step's name, for an app in another language.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name: "Checkout progress".

props.name: steps
props.description: The steps' names, in order: "Cart", "Shipping", "Payment", "Review". Short, one or two words.

Steps.name: Steps
Steps.description:
A numbered list of things to do, in order: a `title` and, under it, a line of `children`. The
numbers are counted by CSS, so `Step`s can sit in a fragment or behind a condition and still run
1, 2, 3. For the way into a product ("install, log in, run"), not for progress: nothing here is
done or current. A wizard's progress indicator is a different part.

`size="lg"` is the steps across a landing page: from `md` they sit side by side in equal columns,
each number at feature size over a large title; below `md` they stack. Use it for two to four
steps.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` a small list down a column; `lg` the steps across a landing page from `md` (two to four).

StickyBar.name: StickyBar
StickyBar.description:
A full-width row that sticks under AppShell's header as the page scrolls: a filter or actions
bar, or a viewer's title and its actions. It sits on the surface with a bottom line and pads its
content as the Container pads a page. Put a `Cluster` in it for the row's layout. It spans its
parent, so it belongs at the top of an `AppShell bleed` page; `FullBleedLayout`'s `bar` is one.

props.name: children
props.description: The bar's content, usually one `Cluster` (`justify="between"` for a title and its actions).

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

storeColourScheme.name: storeColourScheme
storeColourScheme.description: Remember `scheme` for the next visit, or with `"system"` forget the choice so the page follows the system again. A storage error is swallowed, so private mode does not crash.

SubsectionHeading.name: SubsectionHeading
SubsectionHeading.description:
Nested header. `h3`, text-lg/7 semibold, primary text. `size` steps it down to `sm` (text-base,
body size set apart by its weight) for a form-group caption or a dense card, or up to `lg`
(text-xl) for a drawer title; `md` is the default. Under an `AppShell density="compact"` each is one step down. Inside a `Prose`
`md` is text-xl/7 (the h3 of a doc), `sm` text-base/7 (the h4: body size, set apart by its weight)
and `lg` text-2xl/8, the size of a `SectionHeading` there. `lines={1}` keeps it on
one line and cuts it with an ellipsis where its container ends, the full text as the `title`.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; each role has a semantic default.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: lines
props.description:
Show at most this many lines (1 to 4) and end in an ellipsis, as on `Text`: `1` cuts the
heading where its container ends. With plain-text content the full text becomes the `title`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: size
props.description:
The heading's type size: `sm` is text-base/6, `md` text-lg/7 and `lg` text-xl/7 (one step down
each under an `AppShell density="compact"`).

Switch.name: Switch
Switch.description:
An on/off switch for a setting that takes effect at once, usually by saving it to a server: a
native `<button role="switch" aria-checked>`. The caller owns `checked` and flips it in
`onChange`, or gives `defaultChecked` and the switch keeps its own state. A value sent with a
form is a `Checkbox`, not a Switch. Give it a `label`
(the whole label is the click target), or in a table cell leave the label out and name it with
`aria-label`. `hint` is a muted line under the label; `error` adds a red line under it, with an alert
icon, and makes the switch `aria-invalid` and red-edged. The note is the switch's
`aria-describedby`. `size` is `sm`, `md` (the default) or `lg`. `busy` is for the save in
flight: clicks and keys do nothing, and the switch keeps its colour and its focus.
`disabledReason` blocks it, focusable, with the reason as its tooltip. `disabled` is the native
one, washed out. While `loading` the label is drawn and the track is a bone of its size.

props.name: busy
props.description:
The change is being saved: `aria-busy`, and a click or a key does nothing. It keeps its colour
and its focus, which a native `disabled` would lose when the save starts.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether it is on, when the caller owns it (with `onChange`).

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether it starts on, when the switch keeps its own state.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description:
Why the switch cannot be flipped: it washes out and is blocked (`aria-disabled`; a click,
Enter and Space do nothing) while it keeps its focus, and the reason is its tooltip on hover,
keyboard focus and a tap, read out as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A red line under the hint, with an alert icon, announced politely; makes the switch `aria-invalid`.

props.name: hint
props.description: A muted line under the label that says more. It is the switch's `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the switch; the whole label is a click target.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the next value when the person flips it. Not called while `busy`.

props.name: size
props.description: The label's text size and the switch with it.

Table.name: Table
Table.description:
A list of records in a rounded, bordered card. Compose it
from `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableFoot`, `TableRow`, `TableHeaderCell` and `TableCell`. `label`
names the table for assistive tech and is not drawn. Inside a `Card` it is plain: no card of its
own (border, fill and shadow), no tinted head strip and no row hover, only the row dividers. A
column of figures says so once, with `numeric` on its `TableHeaderCell`: its cells then take end
alignment and tabular figures. `size` is the row padding, and the buttons and pills in the rows follow it
(`sm` by default); a field keeps its own `size`. Other props (`id`, `data-*`, `aria-*`) go on the `<table>`. While `loading`, a
body with no rows draws five rows of bones, one per column, and an empty cell draws a bone; the
table keeps its role and its name. A table that fits its box keeps its head row in view (under
the `AppShell` header) while the page scrolls past its rows; one wider than its box scrolls
sideways instead, and takes a tab stop when nothing in it can take focus. `narrow="stack"` draws
each row as a card on a screen narrower than `sm` (a phone), the cells as lines labelled by their column's
title. A click on a sortable title has the table say the new sort aloud, in `sortedLabel`'s words.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the table for assistive tech; it is not drawn.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: narrow
props.description:
What the table does on a screen narrower than `sm` (a phone): `scroll` sideways, or `stack` each row into
a card, the first cell its title and every other cell a line labelled by its column's title.
Stack a table whose rows a person reads one at a time; keep `scroll` for one they compare
down a column.

props.name: size
props.description: The row padding; the buttons and fields in the rows take the same size.

props.name: sortedLabel
props.description:
What a screen reader hears after a click on a sortable title, from the column's title and the
new direction.

TableBody.name: TableBody
TableBody.description:
The `<tbody>`: the rows, each with a line above it and, unless the table is in a card, a fill on
hover. With no rows it draws `empty` (an `EmptyState`, one muted line here) in one cell that spans
every column the head declares; the head stays drawn, so the reader sees what the table holds.
In a loading `Table` a body with no rows draws five rows of bones instead, never `empty`.

props.name: empty
props.description: Shown in one full-width cell when there are no rows: an `EmptyState`.

TableCell.name: TableCell
TableCell.description:
A `<td>`. `tone` is the text weight and colour (see `CellTone`; in a `TableFoot` it defaults to
`strong`); `numeric` sets end alignment and tabular figures (a cell under a `numeric` head cell is
numeric already), `mono` a small mono face. `secondary` is a second,
muted line under the content. One rule for wrapping: prose (a cell of plain text) wraps onto more
lines (never narrower than `min-w-48`, so it scrolls the table before it becomes a sliver); any
other cell stays on one line at its content's width: one that holds a control or a link, and a
`numeric` or `mono` cell (a figure, a code, a type). `lines={1}` caps a long value's width, cuts it with
an ellipsis on one line and, while it is cut, shows the full text in a tooltip on hover, focus and a
tap; the content is then plain text (strings and numbers), since that is what the tooltip shows. `colSpan` passes through: a cell that
spans the row is a full-width panel (a note under a group), and `align="center"` centres it. A
table with no rows takes `TableBody empty`, not a cell built by hand. `span="full"` spans every
column the head declares, so a panel under a row needs no count. `indent` sets a start-aligned cell in by 1 to 3 levels, for a line under a parent row.
While `loading` an empty cell draws one bone, the width of a short value.

props.name: align
props.default: end for a numeric cell, else start
props.description: The cell's horizontal alignment; `center` for a full-width note.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the cell spans; `span="full"` spans them all without a count.

props.name: indent
props.description: Sets the cell in by this many levels (1 to 3), for a line under a parent row. Start-aligned cells only.

props.name: lines
props.description:
`1` caps the width and cuts a long value with an ellipsis on one line; while it is cut, the full
text shows in a tooltip on hover, keyboard focus and a tap. Plain text content only.

Without it, a prose cell wraps down to a floor so it never becomes a sliver, and any other cell
(a `Pill`, a `Switch`, a `Button`, a `TextLink`, a `numeric` or `mono` value) stays on one line
at its content's width.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: A small monospace face for a code or a type, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: numeric
props.default: the column's, from a `numeric` head cell
props.description: A figure: end aligned, tabular figures, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: secondary
props.description: A second, muted line under the content.

props.name: span
props.description: `full` spans every column the head declares: a panel under a row, an open row's detail.

props.name: tone
props.description: The text weight and colour (see `CellTone`). In a `TableFoot` it defaults to `strong`.

TableEditCell.name: TableEditCell
TableEditCell.description:
A `TableCell` whose value opens an editor in place: a cell that holds one `InlineEdit` and
nothing else. It shows `children` as a button with a dotted underline; a click, Enter or Space
swaps it for `renderEditor(close)` and moves the focus into the editor. The editor calls `close`
when it has saved, and Esc closes it: both put the focus back on the value. A press outside it or
Tab out of it closes it too and leaves the focus where it went, so the editor saves its value on
its own change or submit, never on a close. Put the control in the cell itself, not in a popover
of its own, which counts as outside. Takes `TableCell`'s `align`, `tone`, `numeric`, `mono`,
`indent`, `secondary` and `span`. For an edit trigger in a cell that holds other content too, put an
`InlineEdit` in a `TableCell`.

props.name: align
props.default: end for a numeric cell, else start
props.description: The cell's horizontal alignment; `center` for a full-width note.

props.name: children
props.description: The value, shown while closed.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the cell spans; `span="full"` spans them all without a count.

props.name: indent
props.description: Sets the cell in by this many levels (1 to 3), for a line under a parent row. Start-aligned cells only.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button does, for a screen reader, heard after the value: "Edit category". It also names the editor.

props.name: loading
props.description:
The data is not here yet: an empty slot draws a bone of its shape, a filled one draws as usual.
Left out, the part takes the nearest loading layout's or part's; `false` opts it out inside one.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: What a screen reader hears while this part is loading, when its own `loading` is set.

props.name: mono
props.description: A small monospace face for a code or a type, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: numeric
props.default: the column's, from a `numeric` head cell
props.description: A figure: end aligned, tabular figures, and the cell never wraps.

props.name: renderEditor
props.description:
The control that edits the value, drawn while open. `close` shuts it and returns the focus to
the value.

Call `close` once the control has saved: a press outside the cell, Tab out of it and Esc all
close it without a save, so save on the control's own change or submit. The control sits in the
cell, not in a popover of its own.

props.name: secondary
props.description: A second, muted line under the content.

props.name: span
props.description: `full` spans every column the head declares: a panel under a row, an open row's detail.

props.name: tone
props.description: The text weight and colour (see `CellTone`). In a `TableFoot` it defaults to `strong`.

TableExpandCell.name: TableExpandCell
TableExpandCell.description:
The cell that opens and closes the row it sits in: a small ghost button with a chevron that turns
down when `expanded`, named by `label` (visually hidden) and, with a `count`, the count chip after
it, so it reads "Details, 3". The app holds `expanded` and renders what opens under the row: a
`TableRow` with one `TableCell span="full"`, or indented child rows. Give its column a head of
`<TableHeaderCell label="Details" />`. `aria-controls` names what it opens; other props go on the
`<td>`.

props.name: count
props.description: A count chip after the chevron: how many lines open under the row.

props.name: expanded
props.description:
Whether the row is open.

Hold it yourself and render what opens under the row: a `TableRow` with one `TableCell
span="full"`, or indented child rows. Head the column `<TableHeaderCell label="Details" />`.

props.name: id
props.description: The root element's `id`: an anchor, or the target of a `for` or an `aria-describedby`.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's name, visually hidden: "Details".

props.name: onClick
props.description: Opens or closes the row: the app flips `expanded`.

TableFoot.name: TableFoot
TableFoot.description:
The `<tfoot>`: totals and subtotals. Its cells are strong by default and each row has a firmer
line above it, alone and in a card alike. Put it after `TableBody`; a row of it takes
no `tone`.

TableGroupRow.name: TableGroupRow
TableGroupRow.description:
A full-width group header in the body: a tinted row with a `label` that spans every column the
head declares (or `colSpan` columns), and optional `trailing` text at the far end: the group's
count or subtotal, muted. The group's rows follow it. The row is a `<th>`, a heading for the
group, so an action on the group goes in its rows or above the table, not here. For a panel of other content across the
whole row, use a `TableCell span="full"` instead.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the header spans.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's name, at the start of the row.

props.name: trailing
props.description: The group's count or subtotal, muted at the far end of the row.

TableHead.name: TableHead
TableHead.description:
The `<thead>`: small uppercase column titles, on a tinted strip unless the table is in a card.
Holds one `TableRow` of `TableHeaderCell`s. Unless the table is in a card, it stays in view under
the `AppShell` header while the page scrolls past the rows, as long as the table fits its box.

TableHeaderCell.name: TableHeaderCell
TableHeaderCell.description:
A header cell. In the `TableHead` it is a column title, `<th scope="col">`. `numeric` declares a
column of figures, once: the title and every cell under it take end alignment and tabular figures.
A column with nothing to show in its head (a row's actions) takes `label` instead of `children`:
the name a screen reader hears ("Actions"), visually hidden so the head keeps its column. `sort`
and `onSort` make the column sortable: the title becomes a button that fills the cell and asks for
the next direction, the column says where it stands with `aria-sort`, and the table says the new
sort aloud. The app sorts its rows; the table never does. In a body or foot row it is the row's
header, `<th scope="row">`: the cell that names the row (a name, a date), drawn like a `strong`
cell, so a screen reader reads it before each of the row's values.

props.name: align
props.description: The title's horizontal alignment; `end` over a column of buttons, `center` over a centred column.

props.name: label
props.description: The column's name for a screen reader, visually hidden, for a column with no visible title (a row's actions).

props.name: numeric
